definition_zh: 市中心；商业区；市中心的；往市中心
definition_en: the central business area of a city, or in or toward that area
core_image: 高楼挤在河边那一小片亮得最晚的街区
scene: 周末傍晚，公交一路往低处的商业街开，玻璃幕墙反射着夕阳。 We spent the whole afternoon downtown.
sceneCN: 这里 downtown 是「在市中心」（第 1 个义项）；句意是我们整个下午都待在市中心。

pos.zh: 副词：往市中心；在市中心

derivatives.zh: 由 mid-（中部）加 town 构成，义为「城市中段商业区」
由 up 加 town 构成，义为「住宅区、上城」，与 downtown 相对

senses.title: The central business district
senses.definition: the main commercial and business area of a city, usually near its centre
senses.definitionCN: 一座城市主要的商业与办公区域，通常靠近城市中心
senses.example: The old cinema stands in the middle of downtown.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老电影院位于市中心的中段。
senses.why: In North American port cities the town grew downhill toward the harbour, so the low part became the busy centre and kept the name downtown.
senses.whyCN: 在北美港口城市，城区顺着坡往港口方向低下去，低处成了热闹的中心，于是「低城」这个名字就保留下来指市中心。

senses.title: Located in the city centre
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe something in the central business area
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，描述位于中心商业区的事物
senses.example: She works in a downtown law office.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家市中心的律师事务所工作。
senses.why: Once the noun names a district, it can stand before another noun and act as a location label.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个名词能指一个街区，它就可以放在另一个名词前，充当位置标签。

senses.title: Toward the city centre
senses.definition: in the direction of the central business area
senses.definitionCN: 朝着中心商业区的方向
senses.example: The bus runs downtown every twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟公交每二十分钟开往市中心一班。
senses.why: Because downtown was first a direction down the hill, the word naturally kept an adverbial sense of heading there.
senses.whyCN: 因为 downtown 最初就是「往坡下走」的方向，所以它自然保留了「朝那里去」的副词用法。

intro.en: Downtown joins down and town, and its American urban sense grew out of the lower part of a port city.
intro.cn: downtown 由 down 与 town 组合，其美式城市义来自港口城市靠水的那片低处。

items.en: Tun meant an enclosed place or settlement and became the modern word town.
items.cn: 古英语 tun 指圈起来的地方或聚落，后来变成今天的 town。

items.en: Down and town began to appear together for the lower part of a settlement; early examples are rare and dating is approximate.
items.cn: down 与 town 开始连用，指聚落中较低的一片；早期用例稀少，年代只能大致推定。

items.en: In cities such as New York the business district sat near the harbour at the lower end, so downtown came to mean the commercial centre.
items.cn: 在纽约等城市，商业区位于靠港口的那一端、地势较低，downtown 于是固定指商业中心。

items.en: The word spread to other cities and gained adjective and adverb uses alongside the noun.
items.cn: 这个词扩散到其他城市，并在名词之外发展出形容词与副词用法。

items.en: Outside North America it is understood but often replaced by city centre.
items.cn: 在北美之外，人们能理解这个词，但更常用 city centre 来表达。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the town element; the near-meaning group names other parts of a city.
note.cn: 形近组共享 town 这个成分；近义组收的是城市其他区域的说法。

entries.definition: The residential or wealthier part of a city, away from the business centre.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或副词，义为「住宅区、上城」，与 downtown 方向相对。

entries.definition: The central section of a city between downtown and uptown.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「城市中段」，位于市中心与住宅区之间。

entries.definition: A settlement larger than a village but smaller than a city.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「城镇」，是复合词的核心成分。

entries.definition: The central area of a city; the usual British term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「市中心」，是英式英语中最常见的对应说法。

entries.definition: An area where offices and shops are concentrated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「商业区」，强调功能而非方位。

entries.definition: The older central part of a city, often with social problems.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「内城区」，常带社会问题的含义，与 downtown 色彩不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a port city whose business streets lie lower than the houses.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子保留「港口城市商业街比住宅区更低」这个画面。

normal.en: Down plus town is literally the lower town, which was where the shops and docks were.
normal.cn: down 加 town 字面就是「低处的城镇」，那里正是商铺与码头所在。

normal.en: Uptown went the other way and became the quiet residential side.
normal.cn: uptown 往另一个方向走，变成了安静的住宅区。

normal.en: The noun, the adjective and the adverb all point at the same few blocks.
normal.cn: 名词、形容词、副词三种用法，指的都是同一小片街区。

normal.en: In Britain the same place is simply called the city centre.
normal.cn: 在英国，同一个地方就直说 city centre。

normal.en: Downtown keeps its American flavour, which is why it often appears in films and songs.
normal.cn: downtown 带着美式色彩，所以常出现在电影和歌曲里。

abstract.en: Picture towers crowded onto the lowest land beside a harbour.
abstract.cn: 想象高楼全挤在港口旁最低的那片地上。

abstract.en: Picture a bus pointing its nose down a hill toward bright shop windows.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆公交把头朝向坡下明亮的橱窗。

abstract.en: Picture a map where one small square glows while the rest stays grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上只有一小块亮着，其余都是灰色。

examples.en: Most banks have their head offices downtown.
examples.cn: 大多数银行把总部设在市中心。

examples.en: The downtown streets are crowded on weekday mornings.
examples.cn: 工作日的早晨，市中心街道很拥挤。

examples.en: We took a taxi downtown after the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会结束后我们打车去了市中心。

dict_mnemonic.text: down 是「低处」，town 是「城镇」，低处的城镇就是老城商业街，也就是「市中心」。

root: 由 down（向下）与 town（城镇）复合而成。北美港口城市的商业区多位于靠水、地势较低的一端，因此「低处的城区」逐渐固定指市中心商业区；该词义在美国英语中定型，后扩展出形容词与副词用法。无拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: One district name serves as a place, a label and a direction: in downtown, downtown shops, go downtown.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个街区名兼作地点、标签与方向：in downtown、downtown shops、go downtown。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the lowest streets of a port city packed with offices.
core.cn: 核心意象：港口城市地势最低、挤满写字楼的那几条街。

branches.en: DISTRICT: the noun names the whole central business area.
branches.cn: 区划线：名词指整片中心商业区，即第一个义项。

branches.en: LABEL: before another noun it simply marks where something stands.
branches.cn: 标签线：放在名词前，它只标注某物的位置，即第二个义项。

branches.en: DIRECTION: the old downhill motion survives in the adverb.
branches.cn: 方向线：古老的「往坡下」动作残留在副词用法里，即第三个义项。

branches.en: The district and the direction are the same word because people first walked downhill to reach it.
branches.cn: 区划义与方向义是同一个词，因为人们最初就是往下坡走去那里。

branches.en: A downtown office is simply an office inside the downtown district.
branches.cn: 市中心的办公室，不过是位于市中心区划内的一间办公室。

intro.en: Downtown is a compound of two free English words rather than a suffixed form.
intro.cn: downtown 是两个英语自由词组成的复合词，不是加缀形式。

latinIntro.en: Neither half comes from Latin: town is native English and down goes back to an Old English hill word.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不来自拉丁语：town 是英语本族词，down 可追溯到古英语的「山丘」词。

items.example: Down marks the lower position of the district.
items.exampleCN: down 标出这个街区较低的位置。

items.example: Town supplies the settlement being described.
items.exampleCN: town 提供被描述的那个聚落。

items.example: City centre is the British equivalent.
items.exampleCN: city centre 是英式对应说法。

items.example: Business district names the same area by function.
items.exampleCN: business district 从功能上指同一片区域。

derivatives.zh: 由 up 加 town 构成，义为「住宅区、上城」
由 mid- 加 town 构成，义为「城市中段」

definition_zh: 官方的；正式的；公务上的；职务上的；官员；公务员；裁判
definition_en: approved or issued by a person or body with authority; also a person who holds public office or is appointed to enforce the rules of a sport
core_image: 文件末页盖着一枚圆印，印章落下时纸面被压实，留下一个不能随手改动的记号
scene: 桌上摊开的公告还没干透，末尾那枚圆印压着一道浅痕，旁边的人等着看落款的名字。 The official notice was posted before the gate opened.
sceneCN: 这里是「官方的、正式发布的」（第 1 个义项：由有权威者认可或发出）；句意为这份官方公告在开门之前就贴了出去。可辨物件：摊开的公告纸、圆形印章、未干的墨迹、等待的人群。

pos.zh: 官方的；正式的；公务上的；职务上的

derivatives.zh: 由 official 加 -ly 构成，义为「官方地；正式地」
由 official 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「非官方的」
由 official 与 -dom 复合而成，义为「官僚阶层；官场」

senses.title: Approved or issued by an authority
senses.definition: stated, approved or issued by a person or body that has the power to do so
senses.definitionCN: 由有权如此行事的人或机构作出、认可或发出的
senses.example: The official result will be announced at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 官方结果将在中午公布。
senses.why: Latin officialis described what belonged to a duty or a charge; since only a charge-holder could put such a mark on a paper, the adjective came to label whatever carries that authorization.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 officialis 描述「属于某项职责」的东西；因为只有承担职责的人才能在纸上落下这种记号，这个形容词便用来标注凡是带着这种授权的事物。

senses.title: A person who holds public office
senses.definition: a person who holds a position of authority in a government or a large organization
senses.definitionCN: 在政府或大型机构中担任权威职位的人
senses.example: Several officials attended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 几位官员出席了会议。
senses.why: Latin used officialis as a noun for the charge-holder as well, and English kept both jobs under one spelling, so an official can be the sealed paper and the person behind the seal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语也把 officialis 当名词用，指担职的人；英语把两种用法收进同一个拼写，所以 official 既可以是盖印的文件，也可以是印后面那个人。

senses.title: Done as part of one's post or duties
senses.definition: carried out in the capacity of a post rather than as a private person
senses.definitionCN: 以职务身份而非私人身份进行的
senses.example: He signed the letter in his official capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 他以职务身份签署了这封信。
senses.why: Not every official act reaches the newspapers: anything performed within the duties of a post belongs to that post, so the word also labels work done in one's public capacity.
senses.whyCN: 并非每件 official 的事都会上报纸：凡在职位职责范围内完成的动作都归属于那个职位，所以这个词也用来标注以公职身份所做的工作。

senses.title: A person appointed to enforce the rules of a sport
senses.definition: a referee, umpire or other person appointed to apply the rules of a game
senses.definitionCN: 被指派执行比赛规则的裁判、仲裁或其他人员
senses.example: The official stopped the match when the rain grew heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 雨势变大时，裁判中止了比赛。
senses.why: A match needs someone whose charge is the rulebook rather than a seal, and the title for an authority-holder stretches to cover that role without any government being involved.
senses.whyCN: 一场比赛需要一个职责系于规则手册而非印章的人，指「权威持有者」的头衔于是延伸到这一角色，即使完全不涉及政府。

intro.en: Official is the adjective of officium made into a noun as well: it points at whatever belongs to a charge, and at whoever holds one.
intro.cn: official 是把 officium 的形容词同时做成名词：它指凡属于职责的事物，也指持有职责的人。

items.en: Officium named a service, a duty and a post, and every later form of the word carries that core.
items.cn: officium 指服务、职责与职位，这个词后来的每一种形式都带着这个核心。

items.en: Officialis was formed on officium and meant belonging to a duty or a charge, whether of a thing or of a person.
items.cn: officialis 由 officium 构成，意为「属于职责的」，无论说的是事物还是人。

items.en: Old French official kept the adjective and the noun together, and church courts used the noun for a judge who acted on a bishop's behalf.
items.cn: 古法语 official 把形容词与名词一起保留，教会法庭用这个名词指代主教行使职权的法官。

items.en: English took the word first in church and legal settings, where a document or a judge drew authority from an office.
items.cn: 英语先在教会与法律场合使用这个词，那里的文件或法官都从某个职位取得权威。

items.en: Modern English widened it to the state at large, giving official language and official visits, while the sports official carries only the rulebook.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到整个国家层面，于是有了官方语言与正式访问；而体育裁判手里只有规则手册。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the Latin duty-noun; the near-meaning group collects words for formal authority and for the people who hold it.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「职责」名词之上的同族词；近义组收表示正式权威以及掌握权威者的词。

entries.definition: To act at a ceremony with the authority of a post.
entries.definitionCN: 凭职务主持仪式。

entries.definition: Eager to use an authority one does not really hold.
entries.definitionCN: 急于使用并不真正拥有的权威。

entries.definition: A place, a post or a duty inside an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 机构中的场所、职位或职责。

entries.definition: A person who carries a charge in the army, the police or a firm.
entries.definitionCN: 在军队、警队或企业中负有职责的人。

entries.definition: Following the rules of an occasion rather than being casual.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循场合规则、不随意的。

entries.definition: Given the power to act by a proper authority.
entries.definitionCN: 经正当权威授权可以行事的。

entries.definition: An administrative official in a large organization or state.
entries.definitionCN: 大型机构或国家中的行政官员。

entries.definition: A person who enforces the rules of a game.
entries.definitionCN: 执行比赛规则的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a duty turned into a label: whatever bears the mark of a charge is official, and so is the person who holds the charge.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把职责变成的一张标签：凡带着职责印记的事物都是官方的，持有职责的人也是官员。

normal.en: The stem is officium, a duty, so official marks whatever belongs to a duty rather than to a private person.
normal.cn: 词干是 officium（职责），所以 official 标注的是属于职责的东西，而不是属于私人的东西。

normal.en: Latin officialis described the things of a charge, and only the holder of a charge could put that mark on a paper.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 officialis 描述属于职务的事物，而只有承担职务的人才能在纸上落下那个记号。

normal.en: One spelling serves as noun and as adjective, so an official can sign an official paper.
normal.cn: 同一个拼写既作名词也作形容词，所以官员可以签署一份官方文件。

normal.en: Church courts used the noun for a judge acting for a bishop, which is the seed of today's civil official.
normal.cn: 教会法庭用这个名词指代主教行事的法官，这正是今天公务员的前身。

normal.en: A sports official holds a rulebook instead of a seal, yet the charge is of the same kind.
normal.cn: 体育裁判手里拿的是规则手册而不是印章，但所负职责属于同一类。

abstract.en: A seal adds no ink to the facts; it adds permission.
abstract.cn: 印章并不给事实添墨，它添的是许可。

abstract.en: An official answer is one that someone is authorized to give on behalf of others.
abstract.cn: 官方答复，就是某个人被授权代表他人作出的答复。

abstract.en: One word names a person and a stamp because a stamp is only authority made visible.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指人和印章，因为印章不过是权威变得可见。

examples.en: The official result will be announced at noon.
examples.cn: 官方结果将在中午公布。

examples.en: Several officials attended the meeting.
examples.cn: 几位官员出席了会议。

examples.en: The official stopped the match when the rain grew heavy.
examples.cn: 雨势变大时，裁判中止了比赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧飞手」——印章一按，事情就算定了；记住 official 是官方的。

root: 拉丁语 officium（职责）→ officialis（属于职责的）→ 古法语 official → 英语 official；形容词与名词同形，两层都围绕「有职务、有授权」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to a charge; the senses split into the authorized document, the person who holds office, the work done in that capacity, and the rule-keeper of a game.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「属于职责」的东西；义项分为获授权的文件、担任公职的人、以职务身份所做的工作，以及比赛中的执法者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round seal pressed onto the last page of a document, leaving a mark that cannot be quietly altered.
core.cn: 核心意象：文件末页压上一枚圆印，留下一个不能悄悄改动的记号。

branches.en: a round seal pressed into a still-wet notice
branches.cn: 一枚圆印压进还没干透的公告

branches.en: a sign saying closed for the holiday
branches.cn: 一块写着节日停业的牌子

branches.en: clerks walking into a ministry before eight
branches.cn: 八点前走进部委的公务员

branches.en: a letter signed in a formal capacity
branches.cn: 以职务身份签署的一封信

branches.en: a whistle stopping play in heavy rain
branches.cn: 大雨中一声哨响中止比赛

intro.en: The word is a Latin duty-noun with an adjective ending, and English uses the same form as a noun while adding a few endings of its own.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语职责名词加形容词词尾构成，英语把它同样当名词使用，另外又添了几个自己的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin officium, its adjective officialis and the person-noun officiarius together explain why one spelling can be a document, a quality and a person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 officium、它的形容词 officialis，以及指人的 officiarius 合起来解释了为什么一个拼写可以兼指文件、性质和人。

items.meaningCN: 副词后缀：由形容词构成副词

definition_zh: 吸；吮；抽取
definition_en: to draw liquid or air into the mouth or into a space
core_image: 吸管把杯底的液体一点点吸上来
scene: 婴儿正在吮吸奶瓶。 The baby is sucking from a bottle.
sceneCN: 这里 suck 是「吮吸」（第 1 个义项）；句意：婴儿正在吮吸奶瓶。

derivatives.zh: 吸盘；容易上当的人
吸力
吮吸的

senses.title: Draw with the mouth
senses.definition: to draw liquid into the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 把液体吸入口中
senses.example: The baby is sucking from a bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿正在吮吸奶瓶。
senses.why: This is the basic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的义项。

senses.title: Draw out
senses.definition: to pull liquid, air, or dirt into or out of something
senses.definitionCN: 把液体、空气或污物吸入或抽走
senses.example: The pump sucked the water out.
senses.exampleCN: 泵把水抽了出来。
senses.why: The mouth is replaced by a machine.
senses.whyCN: 这里用机器代替了嘴。

senses.title: Be bad
senses.definition: to be very bad or unpleasant, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示很差劲、令人不快
senses.example: The weather really sucks today.
senses.exampleCN: 今天天气真是糟透了。
senses.why: This informal sense is common in speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个口语义项在日常对话中很常见。

intro.en: Suck is an old Germanic word for drawing with the mouth.
intro.cn: suck 是日耳曼语中表示用嘴吸取的古老词汇。

items.en: Sucan meant to suck.
items.cn: sucan 意为吮吸。

items.en: Sucan named the action of a feeding child.
items.cn: sucan 指婴儿吃奶的动作。

items.en: Suck widened to drawing out liquids.
items.cn: suck 扩展为抽出液体。

items.en: Suck also described pumps and machines.
items.cn: suck 也开始描述泵和机器。

items.en: An informal sense means to be very bad.
items.cn: 一个口语义项表示很差劲。

definition_zh: 例外；排除；异议
definition_en: a case that does not follow the rule, or an objection

senses.title: A case outside the rule
senses.definition: a person or case not covered by a rule
senses.definitionCN: 不受某条规则约束的人或情况
senses.example: Everyone must pay, without exception.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都必须付钱，无一例外。
senses.why: One case is taken out of the general rule.
senses.whyCN: 一个情况被从通则中取出。

senses.title: Leaving out
senses.definition: the act of not including someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 不把某人或某物包括进来的行为
senses.example: With the exception of Tom, all agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 除汤姆外，大家都同意了。
senses.why: The phrase marks what has been left out.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语标记被排除的东西。

senses.title: An objection
senses.definition: a strong disagreement with something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的强烈反对
senses.example: She took exception to his tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她对他的语气表示异议。
senses.why: To object is to set your view outside the rest.
senses.whyCN: 反对就是把你的看法置于其余之外。

items.en: Take exception means object.

normalIntro.en: An exception is a case held outside the rule.
normalIntro.cn: exception 是被留在规则之外的情况。

normal.en: To make an exception is to allow one special case.
normal.cn: make an exception 就是允许一个特例。

normal.en: With the exception of means except.

normal.en: No exception means the rule is firm.

normal.en: Take exception to means object to.

abstract.en: Think of one stone left on the wrong bank.

examples.en: This is an exception to the usual rule.

examples.en: They made an exception for her age.
examples.cn: 他们因为她的年龄破了例。

examples.en: He took exception to the unfair remark.
examples.cn: 他对那句不公平的话表示异议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「except（除）＋ ion」——被除去的那一个，就是例外。

root: 拉丁语 exceptio（取出）→ 古法语 exception → exception，核心义「被从通则中取出的特例」。

sensesIntro.en: An exception is a case outside a rule, the act of leaving something out, or an objection.
sensesIntro.cn: exception 指规则之外的个例、排除在外的行为，或异议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one case standing outside a rule.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在规则之外的个例。

branches.en: The special case is the main sense.

branches.en: Leaving something out is the act.

branches.en: Objection sets one voice outside the rest.

branches.en: A special case is what has been left out.
branches.cn: 特例就是被排除在外的那个。

branches.en: Exclusion and objection both divide a group.

latinIntro.en: Latin exceptio comes from excipere, to take out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exceptio 来自 excipere（取出）。

definition_zh: 坚果；果仁；螺母；狂热者；怪人；要点
definition_en: a fruit with a hard shell around an edible kernel, a small threaded metal block used with a bolt, and in informal speech an enthusiast, an odd person or the central point of a matter
core_image: 一枚褐色硬壳裂开，露出里面蜷曲而饱满的果仁
scene: 秋天的院子里，孩子用小石块砸开一枚外壳坚硬的果子，取出里面饱满的仁。 He cracked the shell with a stone and ate the fresh nut inside.
sceneCN: 这里的 nut 是「坚果」（第 1 个义项：带硬壳的可食果实）；句意为孩子用石头砸开壳，吃下里面新鲜的果仁。图中可辨识物件：石块、硬壳、果仁。

pos.zh: 坚果；螺母；狂热者；怪人；要点

derivatives.zh: 由 nut 加 -y 构成，义为「有坚果味的；古怪的」
由 nut 与 shell 复合而成，义为「坚果壳」
由 nut 与 cracker 复合而成，义为「坚果钳」

senses.title: A hard-shelled fruit with an edible kernel
senses.definition: a fruit made of a hard shell around a kernel that can be eaten
senses.definitionCN: 外面是硬壳、里面是可食果仁的果实
senses.example: Squirrels bury nuts before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 松鼠在入冬前把坚果埋起来。
senses.why: The Old English word named the hard-shelled fruit itself, and the picture of a shell protecting a kernel is the oldest layer in this word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词命名的就是带硬壳的果实本身，「壳护着仁」这个画面是这个词最古老的一层。

senses.title: A small metal block with a threaded hole
senses.definition: a small piece of metal with a threaded hole, screwed onto a bolt to hold things together
senses.definitionCN: 带螺纹孔的小金属块，拧在螺栓上把东西固定在一起
senses.example: He turned the nut until the wheel was tight.
senses.exampleCN: 他转动螺母，直到轮子紧固。
senses.why: A nut grips a bolt the way a shell grips its kernel, and English lent that solid enclosing shape to the hardware part.
senses.whyCN: 螺母咬住螺栓，正像硬壳裹住果仁，英语便把这个坚实、包住东西的形状借给了五金零件。

senses.title: An enthusiast, in informal speech
senses.definition: a person who is extremely keen on a particular activity or subject, used informally with a word in front of it
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动或话题极为痴迷的人，非正式用法中前面常带一个限定词
senses.example: My brother is a computer nut.
senses.exampleCN: 我弟弟是个电脑迷。
senses.why: Someone who loves one thing to the point of obsession can be named by that thing, so computer nut turns the object of love into a name for its lover.
senses.whyCN: 痴迷一样东西到极点的人，可以用那样东西来称呼，于是 computer nut 把所爱之物变成了爱它之人的名字。

senses.title: An odd or eccentric person
senses.definition: a person who behaves strangely or foolishly, used informally and often unkindly
senses.definitionCN: 行为古怪或愚蠢的人，非正式且常带不客气的语气
senses.example: Everyone at the office thought the new neighbour was a nut.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室的人都觉得新来的邻居是个怪人。
senses.why: A hard shell also suggests something shut off from others, so a person whose mind seems sealed against ordinary reason came to be called a nut.
senses.whyCN: 硬壳还暗示「与外界隔绝」，于是脑子像密封起来、不按常理思考的人，就被叫作 nut。

senses.title: The central point of a matter
senses.definition: the central or essential part of an argument, problem or plan
senses.definitionCN: 论点、问题或计划中最关键、最本质的部分
senses.example: The committee spent a week getting to the nut of the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会花了一周才触及争端的核心。
senses.why: A kernel is the part worth keeping inside the shell, so the nut of a matter is the small core left after the outer detail is stripped away.
senses.whyCN: 果仁是壳里真正值得留下的部分，于是「事情的 nut」就是剥掉外面那些细节后留下的那点核心。

intro.en: Nut is a native English word with Germanic relatives, and it has a direct Latin cognate in nux, so the shell-and-kernel picture behind it is very old.
intro.cn: nut 是英语本土词，在日耳曼语中有同族词，拉丁语也有直接同源词 nux，所以它背后「壳与仁」的画面非常古老。

items.en: Scholars generally reconstruct a root for nut, related to words for pressing or squeezing, though its exact form is uncertain and not accepted by everyone.
items.cn: 学者一般认为存在一个表示坚果的词根，与「压、挤」的词义相关；它的确切形式不确定，也并非人人接受。

items.en: The Germanic form was a strong noun for a hard-shelled fruit, and it kept the same meaning across the northern languages.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式是一个表示硬壳果实的强变化名词，在北部各语言中意思保持一致。

items.en: Old English hnutu named the fruit and also stood in compounds for nuts of different kinds.
items.cn: 古英语 hnutu 指这类果实，也出现在指不同坚果的复合词里。

items.en: Latin nux named a nut and its kernel, and from it came nucleus, the little kernel at the centre of things.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nux 指坚果及其果仁，由此产生了 nucleus，即事物中心那颗小仁。

items.en: Modern English kept the fruit sense, then added the threaded metal block and the informal meanings of enthusiast and odd person.
items.cn: 现代英语保留果实义，随后加上带螺纹的金属块，以及「迷」与「怪人」这两个非正式义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and derivatives built on nut; the near-meaning group collects words for seeds and for keen interest.
note.cn: 形近组收由 nut 构成的复合词与派生词；近义组收表示种子以及强烈兴趣的词。

entries.definition: Having the taste of nuts, or behaving in a strange way.
entries.definitionCN: 有坚果味道的，或行为古怪的。

entries.definition: The hard outer shell of a nut.
entries.definitionCN: 坚果外面那层硬壳。

entries.definition: A tool or device for cracking nuts open.
entries.definitionCN: 把坚果砸开的工具或器具。

entries.definition: The seed of a plant that ripens underground in a pod.
entries.definitionCN: 一种在地下豆荚中成熟的植物的种子；花生。

entries.definition: The edible part inside a nut or a seed.
entries.definitionCN: 坚果或种子内部可食的部分；果仁。

entries.definition: The small part of a plant from which a new plant can grow.
entries.definitionCN: 植物中能长出新植株的那一小部分；种子。

entries.definition: The small brown nut that grows on an oak tree.
entries.definitionCN: 橡树上结的褐色小坚果；橡子。

entries.definition: A person who is very interested in a particular subject or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 对某话题或活动极感兴趣的人；爱好者。

normalIntro.en: Nut is a native word for a shell around a kernel, and English has kept stretching that shell toward hardware, obsession and a person's head.
normalIntro.cn: nut 是表示「壳包着仁」的本土词，英语不断把这层壳的形象伸向五金零件、痴迷以及人的脑子。

normal.en: Old English hnutu and Latin nux are cognates: two branches of one old word for a nut.
normal.cn: 古英语 hnutu 与拉丁语 nux 同源：同一个古老词分出的两支。

normal.en: Nutty adds -y to nut: having the taste of a nut, and later behaving oddly.
normal.cn: nutty 在 nut 后加 -y：有坚果的味道，后来又指举止古怪。

normal.en: A nutshell is the shell holding the kernel, which is why in a nutshell means in the fewest words.
normal.cn: nutshell 是包住果仁的那层壳，所以 in a nutshell 表示「用最少的话说」。

normal.en: Nutcracker joins nut and cracker, a tool that does exactly what its name says.
normal.cn: nutcracker 由 nut 与 cracker 组成，所说的工具正好做名字里的事。

normal.en: A nut and bolt hold metal together because the nut grips the shaft as firmly as a shell grips a kernel.
normal.cn: 螺母与螺栓能把金属固定住，因为螺母咬住螺柱，就像壳咬住仁。

abstract.en: A nut is a promise that something worth keeping is locked inside something ordinary.
abstract.cn: 一枚坚果是一句承诺：值得留下的东西被锁在平常的外壳里。

abstract.en: One word for shell, hardware and a person's mind shows how English trusts shape more than category.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指外壳、五金件和人的脑子，说明英语更相信形状而不是类别。

abstract.en: The nut of a problem is the part you must reach before anything else can be said.
abstract.cn: 问题的 nut，是你必须先触及、之后才谈得上其他东西的那一部分。

examples.en: Squirrels gather nuts and hide them under the roots of trees.
examples.cn: 松鼠收集坚果，把它们藏在树根下。

examples.en: The mechanic tightened the nut with a long wrench.
examples.cn: 机修工用一把长扳手拧紧螺母。

examples.en: He is a jazz nut who owns hundreds of records.
examples.cn: 他是个爵士乐迷，收藏了数百张唱片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那特」——特别硬的那颗壳里藏着好吃的仁；记住 nut 是坚果。

root: 古英语 hnutu（坚果），与拉丁语 nux（坚果）同源；核心是「硬壳裹着果仁」的形状。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hard shell around something worth keeping; hardware, obsession, oddness and the point of an argument all borrow that shell.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是硬壳包着值得保留的东西；五金零件、痴迷、古怪，以及争论的要害都借用了这层壳。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown shell splitting open to show a curled and full kernel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚褐色硬壳裂开，露出里面蜷曲而饱满的果仁。

branches.en: a squirrel turning a nut in its paws
branches.cn: 松鼠在爪间转动一枚坚果

branches.en: a wrench turning on a bolt
branches.cn: 扳手拧在螺栓上转动

branches.en: a fan naming himself after the thing he loves
branches.cn: 爱好者用自己痴迷的东西来称呼自己

branches.en: a neighbour whose habits nobody can explain
branches.cn: 习惯让人说不清的邻居

branches.en: a long argument reduced to one sentence
branches.cn: 长争论被压缩成一句话

intro.en: Nut carries no prefix or suffix in its plain form; its family grew by compounding with shell, cracker and pea, and by the adjective ending -y.
intro.cn: nut 本身不带前缀或后缀；它的同族词靠与 shell、cracker、pea 复合，以及形容词后缀 -y 生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin nux and nucleus are recorded and are direct cognates of the English word, which makes this a native word with a visible Latin twin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nux 与 nucleus 有记录，且与英语这个词直接同源，这使一个本土词罕见地拥有可见的拉丁「双胞胎」。

definition_zh: 网；网状物；网络；净的；净赚；用网捕
definition_en: a material woven from threads with holes between them; the internet; remaining after all deductions; to catch or gain as a clear amount
core_image: 河湾浅水处张着一张旧渔网，网眼一格一格，兜住几条银色的鱼
scene: 天刚亮，河湾的浅水处张着一张旧渔网，网脚用石块压住。 A fishing net hung across the narrow channel, and the water flowed through it.
sceneCN: 这里是「网」（第 1 个义项：用线编成、带网眼用来兜住东西的器物）；句意为一张渔网横挂在狭窄的水道上，水从网眼流过去。图中可辨识物件：河湾、渔网、压网的石块、银色的鱼。

derivatives.zh: 由 net 加 -ing 构成，义为「网；网材料」
由 net 与 work 复合而成，义为「网络；网状系统」
由 net 加 -ed 构成，义为「用网制成的；网状的」

senses.title: A woven mesh for catching or holding things
senses.definition: a material made of threads woven with gaps between them, used to catch fish, carry goods or stop things from falling
senses.definitionCN: 用线编成、留有网眼的材料，用来捕鱼、装货或防止东西坠落
senses.example: A fishing net hung across the narrow channel, and the water flowed through it.
senses.exampleCN: 一张渔网横挂在狭窄的水道上，水从网眼流过去。
senses.why: Old English nett named a woven trap of cords with deliberate gaps, and the gap matters as much as the cord: water passes through while fish are held back.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nett 指用绳线编成、特意留出缺口的捕捉器，缺口与绳线同样重要：水能穿过，鱼却被拦住。

senses.title: The internet, especially as a place people enter
senses.definition: the worldwide computer network, used informally as a place people visit for information or contact
senses.definitionCN: 全球计算机网络，口语中当作人们去获取信息或联络的场所
senses.example: She spends an hour on the net every morning before work.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上上班前都要在网络上看一个小时。
senses.why: A mesh joins many separate points without needing one single path, which is exactly how a computer network links machines, so the old word for a woven trap became the name of a system with no centre.
senses.whyCN: 网把许多分散的点连起来，不需要唯一的一条路径，计算机网络连接机器正是这样；于是那个古老的编织捕捉器之名，成了一个没有中心的系统的名称。

senses.title: Remaining after all deductions
senses.definition: left over after costs, taxes or other amounts have been taken away
senses.definitionCN: 扣去成本、税项或其他数额之后剩下的
senses.example: The company reported a net profit of two million pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 公司公布了二百万英镑的净利润。
senses.why: This adjective is a different word from the mesh: French net meant clean and clear, and a clear amount is one with every deduction washed out of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词与「网」是不同的词：法语 net 意为干净、清楚，而「干净」的数额就是把每一项扣除都洗掉之后剩下的数。

senses.title: To catch in a net
senses.definition: to catch a fish, bird or ball in a net
senses.definitionCN: 用网兜住鱼、鸟或球
senses.example: They netted three fish before the tide turned.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水转向之前，他们用网捕到了三条鱼。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb without adding a syllable, and the action is simply doing what the object was made for; netting a ball is the goalkeeper using the mesh as intended.
senses.whyCN: 名词不添一个音节就变成动词，动作不过是让器物做它本来被造出来要做的事；门将把球收进网里，就是按设计使用那张网。

senses.title: To gain as a clear amount
senses.definition: to earn or obtain an amount after everything else has been taken away
senses.definitionCN: 扣去其他一切之后赚到或得到某个数额
senses.example: The sale netted the family enough to repair the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔买卖让这家人净赚了足够修屋顶的钱。
senses.why: Once net names the clean remainder, the verb can name the act of arriving at it, so money, points and results are all said to be netted when nothing is given back.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 net 指「干净的剩余」，动词就能指得到这个剩余的动作；于是钱、分数与结果在无须退还时都可以说被 netted。

intro.en: Net joins two stories: a Germanic word for a woven mesh and a French word for a clean remainder that came from Latin brightness, and English wrote both with the same three letters.
intro.cn: net 合并了两个来历：一个指编织网眼的日耳曼词，和一个经法语、来自拉丁语「光亮」的「干净剩余」；英语把两者写成了同样的三个字母。

items.en: Nett was the ordinary word for a mesh of cords used in hunting and fishing, and it also named cloth woven in the same way.
items.cn: nett 是狩猎与捕鱼所用绳网的通称，也指按同样方式织成的布。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form natja- stands behind nett and its cousins in the other Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式 natja- 位于 nett 及其他日耳曼语同族词的背后。

items.en: A second source reached English through French: Latin nitidus meant clean and bright, and Old French net meant clear and unspoiled.
items.cn: 第二个来源经法语进入英语：拉丁语 nitidus 意为干净、光亮，古法语 net 意为清楚、未受污损。

items.en: Middle English kept net for the mesh and also used net for a clear sum of money; the two words looked and were written alike, so they merged.
items.cn: 中古英语用 net 指网，也用 net 指清楚的金额；两个词形与拼写相同，于是合并了。

items.en: Modern English keeps both strands, adds the internet sense, and lets the adjective and verb carry the idea of a clean remainder.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两支来历，添上互联网义，并让形容词与动词承担「干净剩余」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the woven material, the compound built on net, and the French relative for a clean amount; the near-meaning group holds other words for meshes and for the opposite of net.
note.cn: 形近组收编织材料、建在 net 上的复合词，以及表示「干净数额」的法语亲缘词；近义组收其他表示网状物的词，以及 net 的反义词。

entries.definition: Fabric or mesh made of net, also the act of using one.
entries.definitionCN: 用网做成的布料或网，也指用网的动作。

entries.definition: A system of connected people or machines, built from net and work.
entries.definitionCN: 由 net 与 work 构成，指相互连接的人或机器的系统。

entries.definition: Tidy and clean; the adjective shares the French source of the clean-amount sense, though it looks like a short form of net.
entries.definitionCN: 整洁干净的；与「干净数额」义共享法语来源，外形却像 net 的短形式。

entries.definition: The open weave of a net, or any material with regular gaps.
entries.definitionCN: 网的编织结构，或任何带规则网眼的材料。

entries.definition: A network of fine threads, especially one spun by a spider.
entries.definitionCN: 细丝构成的网，尤指蜘蛛结的网。

entries.definition: A frame of crossed strips with regular spaces, closer to a structure than a trap.
entries.definitionCN: 交叉条板构成、留有规则空隙的框架，更接近结构而非捕捉器。

entries.definition: Total, before any deductions, the direct opposite of net in accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 未扣除任何项的总额，在账目中是 net 的直接反义。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic mesh on one side and a French clean remainder on the other, and its senses divide neatly along that old seam.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词一面是日耳曼语的网，另一面是法语的「干净剩余」，各义项正好沿着这条古老的接缝分开。

normal.en: Old English nett meant a woven mesh with gaps, and the gaps are the point: what passes through is as important as what is held.
normal.cn: 古英语 nett 指留有空隙的编织网，空隙才是关键：让什么通过，与拦住什么同样重要。

normal.en: Netting and network both grow from the mesh: one is the material, the other a system joined like a mesh.
normal.cn: netting 与 network 都从「网」长出：一个是材料，另一个是像网一样连接的系统。

normal.en: Net profit is the other word: French net meant clean, and a clean sum has had every deduction taken out.
normal.cn: net profit 用的是另一个词：法语 net 意为干净，而干净的金额已经扣除了每一项。

normal.en: Neat comes from the same French source, so neat handwriting and net profit share a picture of a clean surface.
normal.cn: neat 出自同一法语来源，所以工整的字迹与净利润共享一幅「干净表面」的画面。

normal.en: The verb netted works for both strands: fish are netted in a mesh, and a deal nets a clean profit.
normal.cn: 动词 netted 两支都管：鱼被网兜住，买卖则净得一笔干净利润。

abstract.en: A trap and an accounting term ended up as one spelling, which is why a word can hold water and money at the same time.
abstract.cn: 一个捕捉器与一个会计术语最后写成了同一个拼写，所以一个词能同时兜住水和钱。

abstract.en: The mesh teaches that connection does not need a centre, a lesson the internet inherited from a fishing tool.
abstract.cn: 网说明连接不需要中心，这是互联网从一件渔具继承来的道理。

abstract.en: What is net is what remains when everything extra has passed through, just as water passes through the mesh.
abstract.cn: 「净」的东西就是一切多余之物穿过去之后剩下的，正如水穿过网眼。

examples.en: The goalkeeper caught the ball in the net.
examples.cn: 守门员把球收进网里。

examples.en: She checks the net for the latest news.
examples.cn: 她上网查看最新消息。

examples.en: The deal netted them enough money to move house.
examples.cn: 这笔交易让他们净赚了足够搬家的钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内特」——网眼一格一格，兜住鱼也兜住利润；net 就是网、净的。

root: 网义来自古英语 nett（一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 natja-）；「净的」义经古法语 net 来自拉丁语 nitidus（干净的、光亮的），两个同形词在现代英语中合并。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a woven structure with gaps; the gaps catch fish, link computers, and let a clean remainder emerge after everything else passes through.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个留有空隙的编织结构；空隙兜住鱼、连起计算机，也让其他一切穿过后留下干净的剩余。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old fishing net stretched across shallow water, held down by stones, with silver fish caught in its open squares.
core.cn: 核心意象：浅水里张着一张旧渔网，网脚被石块压住，网眼兜着几条银色的鱼。

branches.cn: 天亮时横挂在水道上的网

branches.cn: 高架钢丝下方的安全网

branches.en: an hour of news read online
branches.cn: 在网上读一小时新闻

branches.cn: 扣去成本后打印出的利润数字

branches.cn: 三条鱼与一笔好买卖

intro.en: The word is a Germanic mesh noun, a French adjective of cleanliness, the Latin brightness behind it, and the English forms built from both strands.
intro.cn: 这个词由日耳曼语「网」名词、法语表示干净的形容词、其背后的拉丁语「光亮」，以及两支长出的英语形式共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The mesh word is Germanic, while the sense of a clean remainder comes from Latin nitidus through French, so the two origins sit side by side inside one spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 「网」的词是日耳曼语，而「干净剩余」义经法语来自拉丁语 nitidus，两个来源并排躺在一个拼写里。

senses.title: The organ in the mouth
senses.definition: the soft movable organ inside the mouth used for tasting and speaking
senses.definitionCN: 口腔内柔软灵活的器官，用于尝味和发音
senses.example: The dog's tongue hung out as it ran.
senses.exampleCN: 狗跑的时候舌头伸在外面。
senses.why: The core image is simply this flexible muscle that every speaker owns.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象就是这块人人都有、灵活自如的肌肉。

senses.title: A language
senses.definition: a language, especially the one a person learns first
senses.definitionCN: 一种语言，尤指一个人最先学会的语言
senses.example: English is a global tongue shared by many nations.
senses.exampleCN: 英语是许多国家共用的全球性语言。
senses.why: Because the tongue produces speech, it came to stand for the whole language.
senses.whyCN: 因为舌头是发音器官，于是用它代指整个语言。

senses.title: The ability to speak
senses.definition: the power of speech, or the way a person talks
senses.definitionCN: 说话的能力，或一个人说话的方式
senses.example: Fear robbed her of her tongue for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 恐惧让她一时间说不出话来。
senses.why: Losing the organ means losing speech, so tongue also means the gift of talking.
senses.whyCN: 失去舌头便失去言语，于是 tongue 也指说话的本领。

senses.title: Something shaped like a tongue
senses.definition: a long thin piece that looks or moves like a tongue, such as a flame or a shoe part
senses.definitionCN: 形似舌头的细长物，如火苗、鞋舌等
senses.example: Tongues of flame licked the old barn.
senses.exampleCN: 火苗舔舐着旧谷仓。
senses.why: Anything long, soft and flickering recalls the shape of a tongue.
senses.whyCN: 细长、柔软、闪动之物都会让人联想到舌头的形状。

intro.en: Tongue is an Old English word from the Germanic family, related to Latin lingua only at the deep Indo-European level.
intro.cn: tongue 源自古英语日耳曼语族，与拉丁语 lingua 仅在印欧语系的深层有亲缘。

items.en: The reconstructed root *dn̥ghwā- meant 'tongue', giving both Germanic and Latin words.
items.cn: 重构词根 *dn̥ghwā- 意为「舌头」，同时衍生出日耳曼与拉丁两支词。

items.en: Tunge meant the tongue and, by extension, speech and language.
items.cn: 古英语 tunge 指舌头，引申为言语、语言。

items.en: Spelling varied as tunge, tonge, and tonge with a g before n.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 tunge、tonge 等，出现 g 在 n 前的写法。

items.en: Spelling settled as tongue, though the g is not pronounced.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 tongue，其中 g 不发音。

items.en: The senses of language and speaking ability remain in daily use.
items.cn: 「语言」与「说话能力」两义沿用至今。

note.en: Words close to tongue in spelling, and words in the mouth-and-language field.
note.cn: 与 tongue 拼写相近的词，以及同属口腔与语言义场的词。

examples.cn: 她忍住没说，避免了一场争吵。

examples.en: He speaks three tongues fluently.
examples.cn: 他能流利地讲三种语言。

examples.en: Tongues of fire rose from the campfire.
examples.cn: 火苗从篝火中升腾而起。
