abstract.cn: 停下工作，也是一种击打。

examples.en: The workers went on strike for higher pay.
examples.cn: 工人罢工要求提高工资。

examples.en: He struck the ball with his bat.
examples.cn: 他用球棒击球。

examples.en: A good idea struck me on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家路上我忽然想到一个好主意。

dict_mnemonic.text: strike 本是一次「打」；工人用停工去打雇主就是罢工，念头打中你就是突然想到，风暴打来就是侵袭。

root: 来自古英语 strican（抚摸、移动），属日耳曼语词；由快速的动作发展出「击打」，再引申出罢工、突然想到与灾害侵袭。

sensesIntro.en: Strike is a blow, a work stoppage, a sudden idea, or a sudden attack.
sensesIntro.cn: strike 是一次击打、一场停工、一个突然的念头，或一次突然的侵袭。

core.en: A hand coming down on a target.
core.cn: 一只手朝目标落下。

branches.en: A bat meets a ball.
branches.cn: 球棒击中球。

branches.en: Workers leave the factory gate.
branches.cn: 工人走出厂门。

branches.en: An answer appears in the shower.
branches.cn: 答案在淋浴时冒出来。

branches.en: A storm reaches the shore.
branches.cn: 暴风雨抵达海岸。

branches.en: Both a strike and a storm interrupt the day.
branches.cn: 罢工与风暴都会打断日常。

intro.en: Strike takes irregular past forms and builds adjective and noun forms.
intro.cn: strike 有特殊过去式，并构成形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: one who strikes, or a forward

definition_zh: 广告；广告宣传；公告、启事；（某事物的）活招牌
definition_en: a paid notice that promotes a product or service, the activity of advertising, a public notice, or something that openly shows a quality
core_image: 报纸整版里被买下的那一小块，只放一张图和一句话
scene: 临街的橱窗整个换上了新一季的海报，路人纷纷停下脚步拍照。 The new advertisement filled the whole shop window.
sceneCN: 这里 advertisement 指橱窗里那张付费的商业广告（第 1 个义项：广告）；句意为这张新广告占满了整个橱窗。

pos.zh: 名词：广告；广告宣传；公告、启事；活招牌

derivatives.zh: 由 advertisement 去掉名词后缀 -ment 所得的动词形式，义为「做广告；宣传」
由 advertise 加表施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告的人」
由 advertise 加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」
本词的英式口语截短形式，义为「广告」

senses.title: A paid notice promoting something
senses.definition: a notice, picture, film, or online item that is paid for and used to promote a product, service, or event
senses.definitionCN: 为推广商品、服务或活动而付费发布的告示、图片、影片或网络内容
senses.example: The new advertisement filled the whole shop window.
senses.exampleCN: 这张新广告占满了整个橱窗。
senses.why: The word is built on advertise, which means turning attention toward something; the notice is the paid means of making that turn happen.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 advertise 之上，意思是把注意力转向某物；广告就是让这次「转过去」发生的付费手段。

senses.title: The act of advertising
senses.definition: the activity or business of making goods known to the public, used as an uncountable noun in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 让公众知道商品的这一活动或行业，在正式书面语中作不可数名词
senses.example: The advertisement of tobacco is now tightly controlled.
senses.exampleCN: 如今烟草广告受到严格管控。
senses.why: The noun can name the whole activity, not just one item: the -ment ending also carries the sense of an action or its result.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能指整个活动，而不只是一则东西：-ment 词尾本来就同时表示动作与其结果。

senses.title: A public notice or announcement
senses.definition: a formal public notice giving information, such as a legal announcement or a notice in a newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 提供信息的正式公开告示，如法律公告或报纸上的启事
senses.example: The court placed an advertisement of the hearing in the local paper.
senses.exampleCN: 法院在本地报纸上刊登了开庭公告。
senses.why: Before the word meant selling, it meant making something publicly known, and that older sense survives in official notices.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「卖东西」之前，这个词表示「让公众知道」；这一旧义仍活在官方告示里。

senses.title: Something that openly shows a quality
senses.definition: in phrases such as be no advertisement for, a person or thing that publicly shows the good or bad qualities of something
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be no advertisement for 等短语，指公开显示某事物好坏品质的人或物
senses.example: That shabby waiting room is no advertisement for the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 那间破旧的候诊室可给这家诊所做不了好招牌。
senses.why: Anything that puts a quality on public view is doing what an advertisement does, without being paid or printed.
senses.whyCN: 凡是把某种品质摆到公众眼前的东西，都在做广告所做的事，只是没有付费、也没有印出来。

intro.en: Advertisement is an English noun formed from the verb advertise plus -ment; the selling sense came later than the sense of public notice.
intro.cn: advertisement 是由动词 advertise 加 -ment 构成的英语名词；卖东西的义项晚于「公开告示」的义项。

items.en: Ad 'to, toward' plus vertere 'to turn' formed advertere, 'to turn toward'.
items.cn: ad「朝向」加 vertere「转」构成 advertere，意为「使转向」。

items.en: Later Latin also used the verb for turning the mind to something, that is, noticing or paying attention.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语也用这个动词表示把心思转向某事，即注意到、留意。

items.en: The verb advertise entered English meaning 'to inform' and 'to turn one's attention'; the noun was not yet established.
items.cn: 动词 advertise 进入英语时意为「告知」与「把注意力转向」；名词当时尚未确立。

items.en: Advertise plus the noun suffix -ment gave advertisement, first for the act of giving public notice and then for the notice itself.
items.cn: advertise 加名词后缀 -ment 构成 advertisement，先指发布公告这一行为，后指公告本身。

items.en: With the growth of newspapers and consumer goods, the commercial sense became dominant; British speech later clipped the word to advert.
items.cn: 随着报纸与消费品的发展，商业义成为主流；英式口语后来把这个词截短为 advert。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word's own family; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of public notice and publicity.
note.cn: 形近组是这个词自己的词族；近义组收其他类型的公开告示与宣传用语。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed, meaning to make something known publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「做广告；宣传」，本词正是在它后面加 -ment 构成的。

entries.definition: The person or company that pays for advertising.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告主、登广告者」，由 advertise 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The industry or activity that produces and places ads.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告业、广告活动」，由 advertise 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A British informal clipping of this same noun, much shorter in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，是本词的英式口语截短形式，口语中短得多。

entries.definition: The shortest everyday word for an advertisement, used in speech and headlines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，是最短的日常说法，多用于口语与标题。

entries.definition: A broadcast advertisement, especially one shown on television or radio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电视或广播广告」，特指播出的一段推销短片。

entries.definition: A public statement of information, with no selling purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公告、通知」，只提供信息，没有推销目的。

entries.definition: A sign or sheet giving information or a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「告示、通知」，指提供信息或警告的牌子或纸张。

entries.definition: Attention given to someone or something by the media, whether paid for or not.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公众关注、宣传」，指媒体给予的关注，付费与否都算。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real structure of advertise plus -ment and the word's older sense of public notice.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用 advertise 加 -ment 的真实结构，以及这个词更早的「公开告示」义。

normal.en: Advertere is 'to turn toward', so an advertisement turns a reader's eyes toward a seller.
normal.cn: advertere 是「使转向」，所以 advertisement 就是把读者的眼睛转向卖家。

normal.en: The -ment ending turns the act of advertising into a thing you can hold: a page, a poster, a clip.
normal.cn: -ment 词尾把「做广告」这个动作变成能拿在手里的东西：一页纸、一张海报、一段片子。

normal.en: The word first meant a public notice, not a sales pitch, and that older sense survives in official announcements.
normal.cn: 这个词最早指公开告示，而不是推销话术；这一旧义仍活在官方公告里。

normal.en: Be no advertisement for means the thing itself shows the bad side of what it belongs to.
normal.cn: be no advertisement for 指某物本身就暴露出它所属之物的坏的一面。

normal.en: British speech cuts the long noun to advert, which is why the two words differ so much in length.
normal.cn: 英式口语把这个长名词砍成 advert，所以这两个词的长度差得这么远。

abstract.en: Picture one square of a newspaper page that has been bought and filled with a single bright picture.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸一整版里被买下的那一小方块，里面只放一张鲜亮的图。

abstract.en: An advertisement is a paid turn of the head: someone bought the moment your eyes moved.
abstract.cn: 广告是一次付费的转头：有人买下了你目光移动的那一瞬。

abstract.en: The same page can sell, announce or warn; money buys the attention, not the belief.
abstract.cn: 同一页纸可以卖货、可以公告、也可以警告；钱买到的是注意力，不是信任。

examples.en: The new advertisement filled the whole shop window.
examples.cn: 这张新广告占满了整个橱窗。

examples.en: The advertisement of tobacco is now tightly controlled.
examples.cn: 如今烟草广告受到严格管控。

examples.en: That shabby waiting room is no advertisement for the clinic.
examples.cn: 那间破旧的候诊室可给这家诊所做不了好招牌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃提斯门特」——阿德买下整页纸，只写一行字：广告。

root: 由动词 advertise 加名词后缀 -ment 构成；advertise 出自拉丁语 advertere「使转向」，所以本词本义是「使人注意的告知」，后来才专指付费的商业广告。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: a paid notice, the act of advertising, an official public notice, and a person or thing that openly displays a quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：付费的广告；广告宣传这一行为；正式的公开告示；公开显示某种品质的人或物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bought square on a crowded page, holding a single picture and a single line.
core.cn: 核心意象：拥挤版面上被买下的那一方块，只放一张图、一行字。

branches.en: THE PAGE: a printed space is bought and filled with a seller's message.
branches.cn: 纸面线：买下印刷版面，填上卖家的信息。

branches.en: THE SCREEN: the same bought attention is delivered as a short film or an online item.
branches.cn: 屏幕线：同样买来的注意力，以短片或网络内容的形式送出。

branches.en: THE ACT: the noun also names the whole business of advertising, not one item.
branches.cn: 行为线：这个名词也能指整个广告活动，而不只是一则内容。

branches.en: THE NOTICE: the older sense of making something publicly known survives in formal announcements.
branches.cn: 告示线：让公众知道的旧义，保存在正式的公告里。

branches.en: THE EXAMPLE: anything that openly shows a quality is doing the word's work without being paid.
branches.cn: 例证线：任何公开显示品质的东西，不收费也在做这个词所做的事。

intro.en: Advertisement is advertise plus -ment, and advertise in turn rests on the Latin prefix ad- and the verb vertere.
intro.cn: advertisement 是 advertise 加 -ment；而 advertise 又建立在拉丁语前缀 ad- 与动词 vertere 之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere and advertere are recorded; -ment goes back to Latin -mentum through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 与 advertere 都有记录；-ment 经法语上溯到拉丁语 -mentum。

items.example: It joins vertere to form advertere.
items.exampleCN: 它与 vertere 结合构成 advertere。

items.example: The same root appears in convert and reverse.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根还出现在 convert 与 reverse 里。

items.example: It is the source of the English verb advertise.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语动词 advertise 的来源。

items.example: The noun adds -ment to this verb.
items.exampleCN: 名词就是在这个动词后加 -ment。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
an activity or an action in progress
items.meaningCN: 活动，或正在进行的动作

derivatives.zh: 与本词同根的动词，义为「做广告；宣传」
由 advertise 加表施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「广告主」
由 advertise 加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」

definition_zh: 裤子；长裤
definition_en: a piece of clothing worn over the waist and legs, with a part for each leg
core_image: 两条布筒从上边连到腰上，人一迈步就分开又合拢
scene: 衣柜前，他把一条深灰色的裤子抖开，对着镜子比了比裤腿的长短。 These trousers are too long; I shall have them shortened.
sceneCN: 这里 trousers 是「长裤」（第 1 个义项：遮住腰与两腿、各有一条腿管的裤子）；句意为这条裤子太长了，我要拿去改短。两条布筒从腰部垂下正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉词尾 -s 作定语用，义为「裤子的」
加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「穿着裤子的」
加 -less 构成形容词，义为「没穿裤子的」

senses.title: A garment for the legs
senses.definition: a garment that covers the body from the waist to the ankles, with two legs
senses.definitionCN: 从腰盖到脚踝、分两条腿管的衣物
senses.example: He wears grey trousers to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他上班穿灰色长裤。
senses.why: The two legs of the garment make it a plural word in English and in French.
senses.whyCN: 这件衣物有两条腿，所以英语和法语里都用作复数形式。

senses.title: Trousers as part of a uniform
senses.definition: the leg-worn part of a formal uniform, often with a stripe
senses.definitionCN: 正装制服里成套的裤装，常带侧条纹
senses.example: The officer’s trousers carry a red stripe.
senses.exampleCN: 军官的制服裤上有道红条。
senses.why: A uniform makes the legs of one garment a mark of rank, so the plural keeps its force.
senses.whyCN: 制服让这一件裤装成了身份的标记，复数形式因此依旧。

senses.title: The adjective use before another noun
senses.definition: used as an attributive word meaning of or for trousers
senses.definitionCN: 作定语，表示「裤子的」或「用于裤子的」
senses.example: The trouser leg is torn at the knee.
senses.exampleCN: 裤腿膝盖处破了。
senses.why: English drops the final s when the word becomes a modifier, as in trouser leg.
senses.whyCN: 这个词作修饰语时英语会去掉末尾的 s，如 trouser leg。

intro.en: The word comes from French pantalon and its like, but trousers itself is from Irish or Gaelic trews, the older form of the garment.
intro.cn: 这个词的现代形来自「trews」——盖尔语系里指裤子的老词，后受法语形制影响而定形。

items.en: The older form trews, from Irish and Scottish Gaelic triubhas, names close-fitting legwear.
items.cn: 更早的形式 trews 出自爱尔兰语与苏格兰盖尔语 triubhas，指紧身裤装。

items.en: English borrows trews in the sixteenth century for tight hose worn under a tunic.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 trews，指穿在外衣下的一种紧身裤。

items.en: The ending of the word is reshaped after French forms ending in -ous.
items.cn: 这个词的结尾受法语 -ous 一类形式影响而被改写。

items.en: Trousers replaces breeches in the nineteenth century as the ordinary word for long legwear.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，trousers 取代 breeches 成为长裤的通常说法。

items.en: It stays plural though it names one garment, as do scissors and glasses.
items.cn: 它指一件衣物却仍用复数，如同 scissors 与 glasses。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers garments and near spellings, while the near-meaning group names related items of clothing.
note.cn: 形近组汇集衣物类词与相近拼写，近义组列出相关服饰说法。

entries.definition: used before a noun to mean of trousers
entries.definitionCN: 裤子的（定语）

entries.definition: wearing trousers
entries.definitionCN: 穿着裤子的

entries.definition: the clothes a bride brings to a marriage
entries.definitionCN: 嫁妆；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a problem or difficulty
entries.definitionCN: 麻烦；只是开头写法相近，词源不同

entries.definition: trousers made of strong cotton cloth
entries.definitionCN: 牛仔裤

entries.definition: the American word for trousers
entries.definitionCN: 裤子（美式）

entries.definition: short trousers worn in warm weather
entries.definitionCN: 短裤

entries.definition: a garment hanging from the waist, not divided
entries.definitionCN: 裙子

normalIntro.en: Two legs make a plural word, and English keeps the s.
normalIntro.cn: 两条腿让它成了复数词，英语保留了末尾的 s。

normal.en: A pair of trousers takes a plural verb: these trousers are long.
normal.cn: 一条裤子用复数动词：these trousers are long。

normal.en: Before another noun the s usually drops: trouser leg.
normal.cn: 作定语时常去掉 s：trouser leg。

normal.en: Jeans and shorts are the same kind of plural garment word.
normal.cn: jeans 与 shorts 是同类复数衣物词。

normal.en: The older form trews survives in Scottish English.
normal.cn: 更早的形式 trews 仍见于苏格兰英语。

normal.en: Count them with a pair of, never with a single number.
normal.cn: 用 a pair of 计数，不用单个数字。

abstract.en: Picture two cloth tubes joined at the waist, splitting at the knee.
abstract.cn: 想象两条布筒在腰上相连，到膝上分开。

abstract.en: Hear the cloth swish as one leg passes the other.
abstract.cn: 听一腿越过另一腿时布料的沙沙声。

abstract.en: Then think of a wardrobe where one item has two doors.
abstract.cn: 再想衣柜里一件衣物有两个门洞。

examples.en: These trousers need a new button.
examples.cn: 这条裤子得换颗新扣子。

examples.en: He rolled up his trouser legs and waded in.
examples.cn: 他卷起裤腿蹚了进去。

examples.en: The uniform trousers were pressed before the parade.
examples.cn: 游行前制服裤被熨得笔挺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹着死」——裤子太紧，踹下去差点踹着腿。

root: 苏格兰与爱尔兰盖尔语 triubhas（trews，紧身裤装），十六世纪进入英语，词尾后受法语影响改写

sensesIntro.en: The word names one garment in the plural, and the s comes off when it becomes a modifier.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词用复数指一件衣物，作修饰语时末尾的 s 会去掉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two cloth tubes joined at the waist.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条布筒在腰上相连。

branches.en: The everyday pair of senses: the garment and its attributive use.
branches.cn: 日常一对：这件衣物与它的定语用法。

branches.en: The uniform sense, where the trousers mark a rank.
branches.cn: 制服义：这条裤装标志身份。

branches.en: The plain garment sense again, where the cloth is what counts.
branches.cn: 再回日常义：关键在布料本身。

branches.en: The modifier sense again, where the s is dropped.
branches.cn: 再回定语义：末尾的 s 去掉了。

branches.en: The tailoring sense, where cut and press matter on both.
branches.cn: 裁剪义：两者都看重剪裁与熨烫。

intro.en: The word is Celtic in origin, and its English family is built with plain endings.
intro.cn: 这个词源出凯尔特语，其英语词族由朴素词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Its Celtic source has no Latin relatives in English, so the Latin list here stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它的凯尔特语来源在英语里没有拉丁亲族，所以这里的拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: Trouser gives trousers, the garment name.
items.exampleCN: trouser 加 s 成为衣物名 trousers。

items.meaningCN: 用于计两件成对的事物
items.example: A pair of trousers hung there.
Trews are still worn in the Highlands.

items.meaning: a jacket and trousers of one cloth
items.example: She wore a dark trouser suit.
The hotel has a trouser press.

definition_zh: 强加；征收（税费）；把……强加于
definition_en: to force a rule, tax, or burden on people, or to expect someone to accept something difficult without asking them
core_image: 一纸盖了红章的告示被人按在村口木门上，风一吹还在抖
scene: 村口木门上被人用图钉按住一张盖了红章的告示，风吹得纸边直抖。 The town then imposed a new tax on every shop on that street.
sceneCN: 这里 impose 是「征收、强行施加」（第 3 个义项：把税费等硬按到别人身上），句意是镇上随后对那条街上的每家店铺都征收了一项新税。画面里有村口木门、图钉和一张被风吹得发抖的告示。

pos.zh: 动词：强加、强行施加（规则、负担、想法）；征收（税、罚金）

collocations.zh: 占用别人的时间、给人添麻烦
把自己的观点强加于人

derivatives.zh: 征收、强加；强加之物
（形近）给人深刻印象的、宏伟的
叠加、在……之上再加盖一层

senses.title: To force a rule on people
senses.definition: to officially force a law, rule, or limit on people who did not choose it
senses.definitionCN: 以官方力量把法律、规则或限制强加给没有选择余地的人
senses.example: The city imposed strict limits on fireworks during the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 节日期间，市里对燃放烟花实行了严格限制。
senses.why: The heart of the word is putting something on others with force, and rules are the most common burden.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是「用力把东西压到别人身上」，而规则是最常见的负担。

senses.title: To force ideas or burdens on someone
senses.definition: to make someone accept your opinions, or to take up their time and patience
senses.definitionCN: 迫使别人接受你的看法，或占用他人的时间与耐心
senses.example: I do not want to impose my taste in music on the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 我不想把自己对音乐的品味强加给全家。
senses.why: The burden moves from laws to opinions and favours, which is why impose on means to be a nuisance.
senses.whyCN: 负担从法律挪到了看法与请求上，所以 impose on 才表示「给人添麻烦」。

senses.title: To charge a tax or fine
senses.definition: to order that a tax, duty, or punishment must be paid
senses.definitionCN: 下令让人必须缴纳某项税、关税或罚金
senses.example: A heavy duty was imposed on imported sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 对进口食糖征收了很高的关税。
senses.why: Taxation is the state at its most forceful, so this sense keeps the original physical pressure.
senses.whyCN: 收税是国家最用力的时候，所以这个义项仍保留着原始的身体性压强。

intro.en: Impose comes from Latin words for putting something down on top of something else, and the image of laying a burden on a person has survived.
intro.cn: impose 源于拉丁语中「把东西放到上面」的说法，而「把负担压在人身上」这个意象一直保留到今天。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and it underlies dozens of English verbs from compose to deposit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ponere 意为「放置」，英语里从 compose 到 deposit 几十个动词都靠它。

items.en: Imponere added the prefix in, on, and meant to lay something upon or to place a burden on someone.
items.cn: imponere 加上前缀 in「在上」，意为把东西放上去，或把负担压在某人身上。

items.en: Old French shaped the verb as imposer, used for laying on a charge or a duty.
items.cn: 古法语把它变成 imposer，多用于把什么责任或义务压在别人身上。

items.en: English borrowed it as imposen in the fourteenth century, first in the language of church and law.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入，写作 imposen，最初多出现在宗教与法律用语里。

items.en: Later it covered taxes, opinions, and personal inconvenience, giving the modern phrase to impose on someone.
items.cn: 后来它的用法扩及征税、强加观点和给人添麻烦，于是有了现代短语 impose on someone。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the same ponere root; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of forcing.
note.cn: 形近组收同样建在 ponere 词根上的动词；近义组收其他表示「强制」的动词。

entries.definition: To put something out where it can be seen, or to leave it open to harm.
entries.definitionCN: 「暴露、揭露」，同一词根，但前缀相反，方向朝外。

entries.definition: To put parts together into a whole, as in music or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 「组成、创作」，把部分摆到一起。

entries.definition: Grand and impressive in size or manner, from the same ing-form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「宏伟的、给人压迫感的」，是同一动词的 -ing 形式演变而来。

entries.definition: To make people obey a rule that already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「执行、实施」，指让已有的规则真正被遵守。

entries.definition: To make someone suffer something unpleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「使遭受（伤害、痛苦）」，强调让人承受痛苦。

entries.definition: To lay down what others must do, with no discussion.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「发号施令、规定」，不容讨论地定下别人该做什么。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the put-on image behind the Latin root and the fixed English patterns with on.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用词根背后「放上去」的意象，以及英语中与 on 搭配的固定句式。

normal.en: impose is im plus pose, to put on, so a tax is literally placed on people.
normal.cn: impose 是 im 加 pose「放」，征税就是把税放在人身上。

normal.en: The verb nearly always takes on: impose a ban on, impose a tax on, impose on a friend.
normal.cn: 这个动词几乎总接 on：impose a ban on、impose a tax on、impose on a friend。

normal.en: Saying I do not want to impose is a polite way to admit you need a favour.
normal.cn: 说一句「我不想麻烦你」，是一种礼貌地承认自己要开口求人的方式。

normal.en: The adjective imposing looks like a burden but means grand, because a high wall puts weight on your eyes.
normal.cn: 形容词 imposing 看似负担，其实意为「宏伟」，因为高墙会在你眼前压下来。

normal.en: Keep the pair straight: impose means put on, expose means put out.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：impose 是往里压，expose 是往外摆。

abstract.en: Every rule imposes two costs: one on the person burdened and one on the person who must enforce it.
abstract.cn: 每条规则都强加两种代价：一种落在被管的人身上，一种落在必须执行它的人身上。

abstract.en: The word quietly records the direction of power, always downward from the strong to the weak.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄悄记下了权力的方向：永远从强者压向弱者。

abstract.en: A kindness offered unasked can still impose, which is why English keeps the phrase I hope I am not imposing.
abstract.cn: 未被请求的好意也可能构成麻烦，英语因此留有「希望我没有打扰你」这种说法。

examples.en: The government imposed new rules on drivers entering the city centre.
examples.cn: 政府对进入市中心的司机实行了新规定。

examples.en: Please stay for dinner; I hope I am not imposing.
examples.cn: 留下来吃晚饭吧，希望没给你添麻烦。

examples.en: Heavy fines were imposed on factories that poured waste into the river.
examples.cn: 向河里倾倒废料的工厂被处以重罚。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 在上 + pose 放——把东西硬放到别人身上，就是强加

root: 拉丁语 imponere「放在上面」（in「在上」+ ponere「放置」），经古法语 imposer 于中世纪英语时期进入英语，最初用于宗教与法律，后扩展到征税、强加观点与给人添麻烦。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: forcing rules, forcing opinions or inconvenience on people, and charging a tax or fine.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：强制推行规则，把想法或麻烦加给别人，以及征收税费或罚款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped notice pinned to a village gate, pressing its weight on everyone who walks through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张盖章的告示钉在村口木门上，把分量压在每个经过的人身上。

branches.en: THE RULE: a law is laid on people who never chose it.
branches.cn: 规则线：法律被压在从没选择过它的人身上。

branches.en: THE OPINION: taste and advice can be pressed on others just like rules.
branches.cn: 想法线：品味与忠告也能像规则一样压给别人。

branches.en: THE MONEY: a tax is the same pressure measured in currency.
branches.cn: 钱线：税收就是同一种压力用货币来计量。

branches.en: THE POLITENESS: I hope I am not imposing softens a request.
branches.cn: 礼貌线：一句「希望没有打扰你」，给请求垫上一层软话。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: imposition names the act, imposing describes the effect on the eye.
branches.cn: 词族线：imposition 指这个行为，imposing 则描述它落在眼里的效果。

intro.en: The table lines up verbs built on the Latin root ponere, put or place, with different prefixes.
intro.cn: 此表把以拉丁词根 ponere「放置」为底、带不同前缀的动词排在一起。

latinIntro.en: Ponere and its form pos- supply the spine of the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: ponere 及其变体 pos- 是这一整组的脊梁。

items.meaning: to put a burden on others
items.example: They impose a small fee on every visitor.
items.exampleCN: 他们对每位访客征收一点费用。

items.meaning: the act of forcing something on people
items.example: The new imposition angered local traders.
items.exampleCN: 这项新的强制收费惹恼了当地商户。

items.meaning: to put something out in the open
items.example: The article exposed the hidden costs.
items.exampleCN: 那篇文章揭露了隐藏的费用。

items.example: She composed the song in one evening.
items.exampleCN: 她一个晚上就写好了这首歌。

items.example: He proposed a shorter working week.

items.meaning: to put money down for safekeeping
items.example: Deposit the cheque at the counter.

items.meaningCN: 形容词：宏伟的、气势逼人的
items.example: The imposing gate stopped us for a moment.
items.exampleCN: 那扇气势逼人的大门让我们愣了一下。

items.example: The imposed silence lasted a full minute.
items.exampleCN: 被强加的静默持续了整整一分钟。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语动词：放在上面、施加

definition_zh: 特定的；某一个；特别的；讲究的；细节
definition_en: used to point to one specific person or thing rather than any other, special or worth noticing, hard to please about small details, or, as a noun, a single detail of a matter
core_image: 货架前一个人蹲下身，只从一排同样的罐子里挑出标签最正的那一罐
scene: 深夜的茶馆里，一位老客人盯着茶杯，要求换掉这壶已经凉透的茶。 She is very particular about the tea she drinks.
sceneCN: 这里的 particular 是「挑剔的、讲究的」（第 3 个义项：对细节要求高）；句意是她对喝的茶十分讲究。图中可辨识物件：茶杯、茶壶、老客人。

pos.zh: 特定的；某一个；特别的；讲究的

derivatives.zh: 由 particular 加 -ly 构成，义为「尤其；特别」
由 particular 加 -ity 构成，义为「特殊性；细处」
由 particular 加 -ize 构成，义为「详述；逐一列举」

senses.title: One specific thing
senses.definition: used to point to one definite person, thing or kind, rather than to any other
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出确定的某个人、物或种类，而不是别的
senses.example: She had a particular reason for choosing that seat.
senses.exampleCN: 她选那个座位有特定的理由。
senses.why: Particular comes from Latin particula, a small part, so the adjective begins by picking out one small item from a larger set.
senses.whyCN: particular 出自拉丁语 particula（小部分），所以这个形容词的起点，是从一大类里挑出小小的一项。

senses.title: Special or worth noticing
senses.definition: greater or more noticeable than usual, so that attention is drawn to it
senses.definitionCN: 比寻常更大或更引人注意，因而把注意力吸引过去
senses.example: This case deserves particular attention.
senses.exampleCN: 这个案例值得特别注意。
senses.why: What has been singled out from the rest is by definition noticeable, so the word for one chosen item drifts into the meaning of special.
senses.whyCN: 既然是从其余之中被单独挑出来的，它按定义就引人注意，于是「被选中的那一个」滑向了「特别的」。

senses.title: Hard to please about details
senses.definition: demanding and careful about small details, especially about food, clothes or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 对细小之处要求严格、十分在意，尤指对食物、衣着或举止
senses.example: She is very particular about the tea she drinks.
senses.exampleCN: 她对喝的茶十分讲究。
senses.why: A person who notices every small part of a thing becomes exacting about parts, so the same word shifts from the item picked out to the person who insists on picking.
senses.whyCN: 一个人若连事物的每个小部分都注意到，就会对「部分」格外苛求；同一个词于是从「被挑出的东西」转指「非要挑的人」。

senses.title: A single detail of a matter
senses.definition: a single fact or detail about something, usually in the plural, as in the particulars of a case
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事的某一项事实或细节，通常用复数，如案件的细节
senses.example: The report sets out the particulars of the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了协议的细节。
senses.why: When the adjective becomes a noun, the small part it once pointed at stands alone: a particular is one item on a list of details.
senses.whyCN: 当形容词转为名词，它原先指着的那个小部分就独立出来：一条 particular 就是细节清单上的一项。

intro.en: Particular comes from Latin particularis, built on particula, the small form of pars, part; French passed it to English, where it first meant relating to a single item and later also meant fussy about details.
intro.cn: particular 来自拉丁语 particularis，建立在 pars（部分）的小称 particula 之上；经法语进入英语，先指「与单项有关的」，后来又指「对细节挑剔的」。

items.en: Pars meant a part or a share, and nearly every later English word in this family begins there.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、份额，这一族英语词几乎都从这里出发。

items.en: Particula, the small form of pars, named a tiny piece, and its adjective particularis pointed to one such piece.
items.cn: particula 是 pars 的小称，指极小的部分，其形容词 particularis 就指向这样的一小块。

items.en: Particularis described what belongs to a single item rather than to the whole class.
items.cn: particularis 描述属于某一个单项、而非整个类别的东西。

items.en: Old French kept the word as particulier, meaning individual or specific, and passed it into English.
items.cn: 古法语保留为 particulier，意为个别的、特定的，并把它传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the sense of one specific item, adds the sense of special attention, and develops the noun particulars for details.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「特定的一项」，加上「格外注意」的意思，又发展出名词 particulars 表示细节。

note.en: The look-alike group puts the whole part family in view, so particular is not confused with partial or partly; the near-meaning group gathers words for one exact item, for fussiness and for details.
note.cn: 形近组把整个 part 一族摆在一起，避免把 particular 与 partial、partly 弄混；近义组收表示「特定的某一项」「挑剔」与「细节」的词。

entries.definition: Very or especially, used to single something out for emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 非常、尤其，用来把某事单独拎出来强调。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter; from Latin particula.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒；出自拉丁语 particula。

entries.definition: Covering only a part, or favouring one side.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的，或偏袒一方的。

entries.definition: A wrapped package or a plot of land, from the same small Latin piece.
entries.definitionCN: 包裹或一块地，出自同一个拉丁语「小块」。

entries.definition: Clearly defined and exact, not general.
entries.definitionCN: 明确具体的，而非笼统的。

entries.definition: Different from what is usual and worth attention.
entries.definitionCN: 与寻常不同、值得注意的。

entries.definition: Hard to please, especially about small details.
entries.definitionCN: 难以取悦的，尤指对细节挑剔。

entries.definition: A single small fact or feature of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事中的一项细小事实或特征。

normalIntro.en: Particular points at one small piece picked out of a set, and its hooks follow that piece into special notice, into fussiness and finally into a written item.
normalIntro.cn: particular 指向从一类中挑出的那一小块，记忆钩子顺着这一小块，走到「格外注意」，再走到「挑剔」，最后落到纸面上的一项。

normal.en: Particular and partial both come from Latin pars, but particular picks one item out, while partial describes only a part of it.
normal.cn: particular 与 partial 都出自拉丁语 pars，但 particular 是挑出某一项，partial 则是只占某物的一部分。

normal.en: In particular singles out one case from many, which is exactly what the adjective does on its own.
normal.cn: in particular 从许多当中单独拎出一例，这正是这个形容词本身的动作。

normal.en: Particular about keeps the same act of picking: a fussy person inspects every small part before choosing.
normal.cn: particular about 保留了同一个「挑」的动作：挑剔的人在选之前把每个小处都看一遍。

normal.en: As a noun, particulars are the separate items of a case, each one a small part written down.
normal.cn: 作名词时，particulars 是一件事的各个单项，每一条都是记下来的一个小部分。

normal.en: Particularly is the adverb and usually means especially, not in a partial way.
normal.cn: particularly 是副词，通常意为「尤其」，而不是「以部分的方式」。

abstract.en: A word that can mean both specific and fussy suggests that attention to detail and being hard to please are one habit seen from two sides.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能表示「特定的」又能表示「挑剔的」，说明关注细节与难以取悦是同一个习惯的两面。

abstract.en: To call something particular is to say it has been separated from its class, and separation is the first step toward value.
abstract.cn: 把某物称作 particular，就是说它已从同类中分离出来，而分离正是价值的第一步。

abstract.en: The noun particulars turns attention into a list, which is how a habit of noticing becomes a document.
abstract.cn: 名词 particulars 把注意力变成一张清单，注意到细节的习惯就这样成了一份文件。

examples.en: She had a particular reason for choosing that seat.
examples.cn: 她选那个座位有特定的理由。

examples.en: She is very particular about the tea she drinks.
examples.cn: 她对喝的茶十分讲究。

examples.en: The report sets out the particulars of the agreement.
examples.cn: 报告列出了协议的细节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕剔」——挑水果的人怕剔得不干净，一个个翻看；记住 particular 是「特定的」，也是「挑剔的」。

root: 拉丁语 pars（部分）经小称 particula 派生 particularis（属于单项的），再经古法语 particulier 进入英语；与 partial、partly、particle 同出 part，但 particular 走的是「挑出单项—格外注意—对细节挑剔」这一路。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one small piece picked out of a set; the senses divide into the specific item, the special notice it draws, the fussiness of a careful chooser, and the written detail.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从一类中挑出的那一小块；义项按「特定的那一项」「因此得到的格外注意」「挑剔者的苛求」「落到纸面的细节」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone stooping before a shelf to pick the one jar whose label sits perfectly straight.
core.cn: 核心意象：货架前一个人蹲下身，只从一排同样的罐子里挑出标签最正的那一罐。

branches.en: a single seat chosen for a private reason
branches.cn: 因私人理由选定的一个座位

branches.en: one jar taken from a row of identical jars
branches.cn: 从一排同样的罐子里取出的一罐

branches.en: a footnote that asks for closer reading
branches.cn: 要求读者细看的一条脚注

branches.en: a host who tastes the tea before serving it
branches.cn: 上茶前先尝一口的主人

branches.en: a contract read out item by item
branches.cn: 逐条念出的合同

intro.en: Latin pars and its small form particula sit under a Latin adjective, French reshapes it, and English adds three endings for the adverb, the noun of quality and the verb.
intro.cn: 拉丁语 pars 及其小称 particula 托起一个拉丁形容词，法语改变了它的形状，英语再加三个词缀，造出副词、表性质的名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars, particula and particularis are all recorded, so this word has a documented Latin ancestry shared with partial, partly and parcel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pars、particula 与 particularis 均有记录，因此这个词有据可查的拉丁世系，并与 partial、partly、parcel 同源。

definition_zh: 然而；尽管如此；不过
definition_en: in spite of that; however; used to introduce a statement that stands despite what came before
core_image: 门上挂着“禁止进入”的牌子，人还是推门走了进去
scene: 小路封了，一半还泡着水，徒步者却还是跨过告示牌继续走。 The trail is closed and half flooded; nevertheless, a hiker steps past the sign and walks on.
sceneCN: 这里 nevertheless 是「尽管如此、仍然」（第 1 个义项：让步之后仍然成立）；句意：步道已经封闭、有一半被水淹，尽管如此，一名徒步者还是绕过告示牌继续往前走。图中可辨识物件：封闭告示牌、积水步道、徒步者的登山杖、黄黑警示带；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 然而；尽管如此；不过（连接性副词，承接前文并转折）

collocations.zh: 尽管如此，事实仍然不变

derivatives.zh: 尽管如此（同构的并列复合词，用 none 代替 never）
从不；决不（构词成分，此处原义为“一点也不”）
曾经；无论何时（never 的第二成分）
更少的；更少地（构词成分，比较级）
除非（同出 less 的复合连词）
减少；减轻（less 加 -en 构成的动词）

senses.title: In spite of that: opening a sentence against expectation
senses.titleCN: 尽管如此：开门见山地逆着预期说
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to say that what follows is true in spite of what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，表示接下来的内容尽管有前文所说的情况仍然成立
senses.example: The hotel was full. Nevertheless, we found a room nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆客满了。尽管如此，我们还是在附近找到了一间房。
senses.why: Nevertheless is never plus the less, literally 'not any the less'. What came before does not make the next statement any smaller, so the sentence opens by refusing to be reduced.
senses.whyCN: nevertheless 是 never 加 the less，字面是“一点也不因此减少”。前文并没有让后一句变小，所以这个句子一开口就拒绝被削减。

senses.title: Joining two clauses after a semicolon
senses.definition: used after a semicolon to link two clauses and mark the second as a contrast
senses.definitionCN: 用于分号之后连接两个小句，并标记后一句为转折
senses.example: The evidence was thin; nevertheless, the jury convicted.
senses.exampleCN: 证据薄弱；尽管如此，陪审团仍判定有罪。
senses.why: As a conjunctive adverb it carries the contrast across the punctuation. The 'not any the less' still measures the second clause against the first.
senses.whyCN: 作为连接性副词，它把转折跨过标点带过去。“一点也不因此减少”仍在用前一句来衡量后一句。

senses.title: After but: the doubled contrast
senses.titleCN: 跟在 but 之后：双重的转折
senses.definition: used with but to add emphasis, as in 'cheap but nevertheless good'
senses.definitionCN: 与 but 连用以加强转折，如 cheap but nevertheless good
senses.example: The plan was expensive but nevertheless worth every penny.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划很贵，但尽管如此，每一分钱都值得。
senses.why: But already turns the sentence; nevertheless adds that the earlier fact does not reduce the later one. The two markers reinforce rather than contradict each other.
senses.whyCN: but 已经让句子转向；nevertheless 再补上一层：前面的事实并不能削减后面的事实。两个标记是相互加强，而不是相互矛盾。

senses.title: At the end: a trailing afterthought
senses.titleCN: 放在句尾：事后的补一句
senses.definition: placed at the end of a clause to add a delayed contrast, often after a pause
senses.definitionCN: 放在小句末尾，补充一个迟来的转折，常出现在停顿之后
senses.example: It was a foolish plan. He went ahead, nevertheless.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个愚蠢的计划。他还是照做了，尽管如此。
senses.why: The word can trail because the comparison is still live: the action is measured against the warning and is 'none the less' for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以拖在句尾，因为比较仍然有效：行动相对于警告被衡量，而它“并未因此减少”。

senses.title: Academic concession: grant the objection, keep the claim
senses.titleCN: 学术让步：承认异议，保留论点
senses.definition: used in argument to admit a limitation and still maintain the main claim
senses.definitionCN: 用于论证中，承认某项局限，同时仍然坚持主要论点
senses.example: The sample is small; nevertheless, the result is suggestive.
senses.exampleCN: 样本很小；尽管如此，这一结果仍有提示意义。
senses.why: The concession lowers the claim's strength, and nevertheless says the claim is not lowered by that amount. It is the written form of 'none the less'.
senses.whyCN: 让步降低了论点的强度，而 nevertheless 说论点并没有因此降低那么多。它就是书面语里的“none the less”。

senses.title: Personal admission: I knew, and did it anyway
senses.titleCN: 个人承认：我知道，可我还是做了
senses.definition: used to admit a fault or risk and still report the action taken
senses.definitionCN: 用于承认过错或风险，却仍然陈述已经采取的行动
senses.example: I knew the risk; nevertheless, I signed.
senses.exampleCN: 我知道有风险；尽管如此，我还是签了。
senses.why: Here the first clause is self-criticism. Nevertheless refuses to let the admission cancel the act, so the person owns both at once.
senses.whyCN: 这里前一句是自我批评。nevertheless 不让这份承认取消行动，于是这个人同时承认了两件事。

senses.title: Formal register: the steady voice of statutes
senses.titleCN: 正式语体：法条里沉稳的声音
senses.definition: used in legal, official, and technical prose as a formal alternative to 'but' or 'however'
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、公文与技术写作中作为 but 或 however 的正式替代
senses.example: The notice was defective; nevertheless, it had legal effect.
senses.exampleCN: 该通知存在瑕疵；尽管如此，它仍具有法律效力。
senses.why: The compound is long and steady, and its 'none the less' logic suits rules that survive exceptions. Formal prose prefers it to a bare but.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词长而稳，其“并未减少”的逻辑正合那些在例外之后仍然存活的规则。正式写作偏爱它，而不是光秃秃的 but。

senses.title: Narrative: obstacles listed, outcome unchanged
senses.titleCN: 叙事：障碍列举完，结果不变
senses.definition: used in storytelling after a list of difficulties to show the result still happened
senses.definitionCN: 在叙事中用于列举困难之后，表示结果仍然发生
senses.example: Rain, delays and lost luggage — nevertheless, they arrived on time.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨、延误、行李丢失——尽管如此，他们还是准时到了。
senses.why: Each obstacle would normally count against the outcome. The word gathers them and says the outcome is none the less for all of them.
senses.whyCN: 每一项障碍通常都会对结果不利。这个词把它们收拢起来，说结果并没有因为这一切而减少。

senses.title: Emphatic: after an extreme list, the result still stands
senses.titleCN: 强调：极端情况之后，结果仍然成立
senses.definition: used after the strongest possible objection to insist that the result stands
senses.definitionCN: 用于最强的反对意见之后，坚持结果仍然成立
senses.example: Every forecast said failure; nevertheless, the launch succeeded.
senses.exampleCN: 所有预测都说会失败；尽管如此，发射还是成功了。
senses.why: The stronger the objection, the more the 'not any the less' has to do. Here the word is close to 'against all of it'.
senses.whyCN: 反对越强，“一点也不因此减少”要做的功就越大。这里的词义接近“对抗这一切”。

senses.title: The fixed frame: it is nevertheless true that
senses.titleCN: 固定框架：it is nevertheless true that
senses.definition: used in the frame 'it is nevertheless true that' to affirm a fact after doubt has been raised
senses.definitionCN: 用于 it is nevertheless true that 这一框架，在被质疑之后仍然肯定某一事实
senses.example: It is nevertheless true that the method saved lives.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管如此，这个方法确实救过人命，这一点是真的。
senses.why: The frame places truth itself on the far side of the contrast: whatever was argued, the fact is none the less true.
senses.whyCN: 这个框架把“真”本身放到转折的另一边：无论前面争论了什么，事实并未因此而不真。

intro.en: Nevertheless began as the phrase never the less, written neuer þe lesse in the early 14c. and joined into one word by the mid-14c. Its never does not mean 'never' but 'not at all, none the', as in never the wiser.
intro.cn: nevertheless 起初是短语 never the less，14 世纪早期写作 neuer þe lesse，到 14 世纪中期合成一词。其中的 never 不是“永不”，而是“一点也不、none the”，如 never the wiser。

items.en: First recorded in the early 14c. as the phrase neuer þe lesse, still written in separate parts.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪早期，写作短语 neuer þe lesse，各部分仍分开书写。

items.en: By the mid-14c. the parts are joined as neuerþeles, and the word begins to work as a single adverb.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪中期，各部分合成 neuerþeles，这个词开始作为单一副词使用。

items.en: Middle English also had neverthelater, never-less, ner-the-less, never-later and not-the-less, all built on the same 'none the less' pattern.
items.cn: 中古英语还有 neverthelater、never-less、ner-the-less、never-later、not-the-less 等变体，都建立在同一个“none the less”模式上。

items.en: Never comes from Old English næfre, itself ne 'not' plus æfre 'ever'.
items.cn: never 来自古英语 næfre，本身由 ne“不”加 æfre“曾经”构成。

items.en: Modern English keeps nevertheless beside nonetheless; the two are parallel compounds, one with never and one with none.
items.cn: 现代英语让 nevertheless 与 nonetheless 并存；两者是并列复合词，一个用 never，一个用 none。

note.en: The first group shares the never-the-less shape or its parts, the second shares the contrastive meaning.
note.cn: 第一组共享 never-the-less 的结构或其组成部分，第二组共享转折的词义。

entries.definition: in spite of that. It is built exactly like nevertheless but with none instead of never, and the two are interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管如此。它的构造与 nevertheless 完全相同，只是用 none 代替 never，两者可以互换。

entries.definition: the older phrase written in separate words. It shows the literal parts: never, the, less.
entries.definitionCN: 分开书写的较早短语。它显示了这个词的字面成分：never、the、less。

entries.definition: an obsolete variant of nevertheless, built with later instead of less. It shows how freely the pattern was varied.
entries.definitionCN: nevertheless 的废弃变体，用 later 而不是 less。它说明这个模式当年被替换得多么自由。

entries.definition: in whatever way, or used to introduce a contrast. It is the general-purpose connector, while nevertheless is heavier and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 无论如何；然而。它是通用连接词，而 nevertheless 更重、更正式。

entries.definition: in spite of; despite. It often works as a preposition or a formal connector, and is even heavier than nevertheless.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管；虽然。它常作介词或正式连接词，比 nevertheless 还要重。

entries.definition: in spite of that, used in speech. It carries the same turn but sounds conversational rather than written.
entries.definitionCN: 即使如此。它带有同样的转折，但听起来是口语而非书面语。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: never here means 'not at all', less is a comparative, and the Middle English variants all repeat the same pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：这里的 never 意为“一点也不”，less 是比较级，而中古英语的各种变体都重复同一个模式。

normal.en: Never in this word is not 'never': it means 'not at all, none the', as in never the wiser or never the worse.
normal.cn: 这个词里的 never 不是“永不”：它意为“一点也不、none the”，如 never the wiser、never the worse。

normal.en: the less is a comparative. Together the parts say 'not any the less', which is why the later clause is not reduced.
normal.cn: the less 是比较级。合起来说“一点也不因此减少”，这正是后一句没有被削减的原因。

normal.en: Middle English had neverthelater, never-less, ner-the-less and not-the-less, all variations on the same comparison.
normal.cn: 中古英语有 neverthelater、never-less、ner-the-less、not-the-less，都是同一个比较结构的变体。

normal.en: Nonetheless is the twin: same building plan, with none instead of never.
normal.cn: nonetheless 是它的双胞胎：同样的建筑图纸，只用 none 代替 never。

normal.en: But nevertheless is a standard frame: but turns the sentence, nevertheless insists nothing was lost in the turn.
normal.cn: but nevertheless 是标准框架：but 让句子转向，nevertheless 坚持这次转向没有损失任何东西。

abstract.en: A door marked NO ENTRY, already pushed half open: the warning is real, and the step is still taken.
abstract.cn: 一扇写着“禁止入内”的门已被推开一半：警告是真的，脚步还是迈了出去。

abstract.en: A line that bends at an obstacle and then continues in the same direction: the bend does not shorten the road.
abstract.cn: 一条线在障碍处弯了一下，然后继续朝同一方向走：弯折并没有让路变短。

abstract.en: A hand pressing down on a box while another hand still lifts it: the weight is counted, and the lift still happens.
abstract.cn: 一只手向下压箱子，另一只手仍把它抬起：重量被算进去了，抬起仍然发生。

examples.en: The instructions were unclear; nevertheless, the team finished on time.
examples.cn: 说明不清楚；尽管如此，团队还是按时完成了。

examples.en: He was warned about the ice, but nevertheless he walked out onto the lake.
examples.cn: 有人警告过他冰面危险，但尽管如此，他还是走上了湖面。

examples.en: It is nevertheless true that the old bridge has carried the town's traffic for a century.
examples.cn: 尽管如此，这座老桥确实已经承载了小镇一个世纪的交通，这一点是真的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那我也赖着」——尽管被赶、被劝，那我也赖着不走 → nevertheless 尽管如此、仍然

root: 由 never“一点也不、none the”＋ the ＋ less（比较级）构成的复合副词，14 世纪早期写作 neuer þe lesse；never 来自古英语 næfre＝ ne“不”＋ æfre“曾经”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of nevertheless all carry one comparison: whatever was said, the next statement is 'none the less'. The word changes position and register, from sentence opening to trailing afterthought, from academic concession to legal prose.
sensesIntro.cn: nevertheless 的十个义项都带着同一个比较：无论前面说了什么，后一句都“并未因此减少”。这个词改变的是位置与语体，从句首到句尾补语，从学术让步到法律文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed sign on a door that is opened anyway.
core.cn: 核心意象：门上的封闭告示，而门还是被推开了。

branches.en: SENTENCE POSITIONS: opening a new sentence, and joining two clauses after a semicolon.
branches.cn: 句子位置：开启一个新句子，以及在分号后连接两个小句。

branches.en: DOUBLED AND TRAILING: after but for extra emphasis, and at the end as a delayed afterthought.
branches.cn: 加倍与拖尾：跟在 but 后加强语气，以及放在句尾作迟来的补语。

branches.en: PERSONAL AND ARGUMENTATIVE CONCESSION: granting a limitation, and admitting a fault while acting anyway.
branches.cn: 论证与个人的让步：承认局限，以及承认过错却仍然行动。

branches.en: REGISTER AND NARRATIVE: the steady voice of statutes, and obstacles listed before an unchanged outcome.
branches.cn: 语体与叙事：法条沉稳的声音，以及列举障碍后结果依旧。

branches.en: MAXIMUM RESISTANCE: after the strongest objection, and in the fixed frame it is nevertheless true that.
branches.cn: 最大阻力：最强反对之后，以及 it is nevertheless true that 这一固定框架。

intro.en: Nevertheless is a compound, not a suffixed word: never plus the plus less. English keeps the same plan in nonetheless, and the parts survive separately in never, ever, less, unless and lessen.
intro.cn: nevertheless 是复合词，不是加后缀的词：never 加 the 加 less。英语用同一图纸造出 nonetheless，而各成分分别活在 never、ever、less、unless、lessen 中。

latinIntro.en: Nevertheless is Germanic. The Latin entries below are counterparts for contrast: nihilominus and tamen both mean 'nevertheless', and minus supplies 'less'.
latinIntro.cn: nevertheless 属日耳曼语。下面的拉丁词是对照用的对应词：nihilominus 与 tamen 都表示“尽管如此”，minus 提供“更少”。

items.meaning: in spite of that; none the less
items.meaningCN: 尽管如此；并未因此减少（never“一点也不”+ the + less 比较级）
items.example: The road was closed; nevertheless, we reached the village.
items.exampleCN: 道路封闭了；尽管如此，我们还是到了村子。

items.meaningCN: 尽管如此（none“一点也不”+ the + less，与 nevertheless 同构）
items.example: The sample was small; nonetheless, the pattern was clear.
items.exampleCN: 样本虽小；尽管如此，规律仍然清楚。

items.example: He never spoke of the accident again.
items.exampleCN: 他再也没有提起那次事故。

items.meaningCN: 曾经；无论何时（never 的第二成分）
items.example: Have you ever seen the tide come in this fast?
items.exampleCN: 你见过潮水涨得这么快的景象吗？

items.meaning: a smaller amount; not as much
items.meaningCN: 更少的；更少地（little 的比较级）
items.example: This route takes less time than the motorway.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线比高速公路花的时间更少。

items.meaningCN: 除非（由 on lesse“在少于……的条件下”演变而来）
items.example: We will go unless it rains.
items.exampleCN: 除非下雨，否则我们就去。

items.meaningCN: 减少；减轻（less + -en 构成动词）
items.example: The medicine lessened the pain within an hour.
items.exampleCN: 药物在一小时内减轻了疼痛。

items.meaningCN: 较小的；次要的（less 再加 -er 的历史双重比较级）
items.example: The lesser of the two risks was still serious.
items.exampleCN: 两个风险中较小的那个仍然很严重。

items.meaningCN: 永无止境的（never + ending，复合形容词）
items.example: The repairs felt like a never-ending task.
items.exampleCN: 这些修缮活像一项永无止境的任务。

definition_zh: 民族的；种族的；民族风情的
definition_en: relating to a group of people with a shared culture or origin
core_image: 一群人穿着相同的传统服饰，围在一起唱歌
scene: 这个街区住着许多不同民族的家庭，节日时格外热闹。 This neighborhood is home to families of many ethnic groups, and it becomes lively during festivals.
sceneCN: 这里 ethnic 是「民族的」（第 1 个义项：与共享文化或血统的群体有关）；句意：这个街区住着许多不同民族的家庭，节日时格外热闹。

pos.zh: 民族的；种族的；民族风情的

多民族的

senses.title: Relating to a people
senses.definition: connected with a group that shares culture, language or origin
senses.definitionCN: 与共享文化、语言或血统的群体有关
senses.example: The city has many ethnic communities.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市有许多族群社区。
senses.why: The Greek source means nation or people, so ethnic marks what belongs to a people.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源意为民族或人民，因此 ethnic 标记属于某个民族的事物。

senses.title: Traditional cultural style
senses.definition: in a traditional style of a particular people
senses.definitionCN: 采用某一民族的传统风格
senses.example: She wore an ethnic dress to the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一件民族风连衣裙去参加节日。
senses.why: Culture shows in clothing and design, so ethnic also describes that style.
senses.whyCN: 文化体现在服饰与设计中，因此 ethnic 也描述这种风格。

intro.en: Ethnic comes from Greek ethnos, a nation or people, through Latin ethnicus.
intro.cn: ethnic 经拉丁语 ethnicus 源自希腊语 ethnos（民族、人民）。

items.en: Ethnos means a nation or people.
items.cn: ethnos 意为民族或人民。

items.en: Ethnikos means belonging to a people.
items.cn: ethnikos 意为属于某个民族的。

items.en: Ethnicus carries the word into Latin.
items.cn: ethnicus 把词带入拉丁语。

items.en: Ethnic describes peoples and their cultures.
items.cn: ethnic 描述民族及其文化。

items.en: It also describes traditional styles.
items.cn: 它也描述传统风格。

note.en: Ethnic is close to racial and cultural, but focuses on a people and its culture.
note.cn: ethnic 与种族的、文化的相近，但侧重民族及其文化。

entries.definition: ethnic identity
entries.definitionCN: 民族属性

entries.definition: in ethnic terms
entries.definitionCN: 从民族角度

entries.definition: a moral principle
entries.definitionCN: 伦理

entries.definition: relating to race
entries.definitionCN: 种族的

entries.definition: relating to culture
entries.definitionCN: 文化的

entries.definition: relating to a nation
entries.definitionCN: 国家的

normalIntro.en: Ethnic points to a people: its language, food and festivals.
normalIntro.cn: ethnic 指向一个民族：它的语言、食物与节日。

normal.en: An ethnic group shares a culture.
normal.cn: ethnic group 共享一种文化。

normal.en: An ethnic minority is a smaller people within a country.
normal.cn: ethnic minority 指一国之内人数较少的民族。

normal.en: Ethnic food comes from a particular tradition.
normal.cn: ethnic food 来自特定传统。

normal.en: Ethnic identity is the sense of belonging to a people.
normal.cn: ethnic identity 是归属于某民族的意识。

normal.en: Compare ethic: ethic is about morals, ethnic is about peoples.
normal.cn: 对比 ethic：ethic 关乎道德，ethnic 关乎民族。

abstract.en: Picture a table full of dishes from one tradition.
abstract.cn: 想象一桌来自同一传统的菜肴。

abstract.en: Imagine a song sung in a language you do not know.
abstract.cn: 想象一首用陌生语言唱的歌。

abstract.en: Think of a pattern woven the same way for generations.
abstract.cn: 想象一个世代相传的编织花纹。

examples.en: The school welcomes students from many ethnic backgrounds.
examples.cn: 学校欢迎来自许多民族背景的学生。

examples.en: The market sells ethnic food from around the world.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ethnic」听起来像「爱死尼克」——每个民族都有自己的特色，这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 ethnos（民族、人民）→ ethnikos（民族的）→ 拉丁语 ethnicus → ethnic，核心义「属于某个民族及其文化」。

sensesIntro.en: Ethnic first describes peoples and their shared culture, and then the traditional style that comes from that culture.
sensesIntro.cn: ethnic 先描述民族及其共享文化，再描述由该文化而来的传统风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: people in traditional dress singing together.
core.cn: 核心意象：穿着传统服饰的人们一起唱歌。

branches.en: The first sense links a person to a people.
branches.cn: 首要义项把人与其民族联系起来。

branches.en: The second sense describes traditional style.
branches.cn: 第二个义项描述传统风格。

branches.en: Culture shapes the clothing and food people call ethnic.
branches.cn: 文化塑造了人们称为民族风情的服饰与食物。

branches.en: Ethnic identity is a common modern phrase.
branches.cn: ethnic identity 是常见的现代短语。

branches.en: Ethnic design borrows patterns from a tradition.
branches.cn: 民族风格的设计借用传统花纹。

intro.en: Ethnic comes from Greek ethnos, people, with the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: ethnic 源自希腊语 ethnos（人民），带形容词词尾 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Latin ethnicus borrowed the Greek word before English took it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ethnicus 先借入这个希腊词，再传入英语。

senses.title: Important
senses.definition: important enough to have an effect
senses.definitionCN: 重要到足以产生影响
senses.example: This is a significant discovery.

senses.why: This is the basic importance sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的重要性义项。

senses.title: Full of meaning
senses.definition: carrying a meaning that is not stated openly
senses.definitionCN: 带着未明说的含义
senses.example: She gave him a significant look.
senses.exampleCN: 她意味深长地看了他一眼。
senses.why: A look can carry a message.
senses.whyCN: 一个眼神也能传递信息。

senses.title: Large enough to be noticed

senses.exampleCN: 销量有显著上升。
senses.why: Numbers can be important by size.

intro.cn: significant 来自一个意为「做记号」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: Significare meant to show by signs.

items.en: Significans meant making signs or meaning.
items.cn: significans 意为做记号或表示含义。

items.en: English borrowed it through French.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入这个词。

items.en: The sense of important became common.
items.cn: 「重要的」这一含义变得普遍。

items.en: The word also described clear differences.
items.cn: 这个词也用来描述明显的差异。

note.en: Significant is compared with similar-looking words and with words for importance.
note.cn: 把 significant 与形近词以及表示重要的词作比较。

entries.definition: a mark with meaning
entries.definitionCN: 标志

entries.definition: having a serious or useful meaning
entries.definitionCN: 有意义的

entries.definition: worth noticing

root: 源自拉丁语 significans（表明含义的），核心义「有分量的、值得注意的」。

sensesIntro.en: Significant means important, meaningful, or noticeably large.
sensesIntro.cn: significant 意为重要的、意味深长的或显著的。

core.en: Something that leaves a noticeable mark.

branches.en: The discovery changes the field.

branches.en: A look says more than words.
branches.cn: 一个眼神胜过言语。

branches.en: Size can make a change important.

branches.en: Meaning can be shown or measured.

latinIntro.cn: significant 来自拉丁语 significans（做记号的）。

definition_zh: 预订；保留；储备（物）；矜持
definition_en: to keep something for future use, or a supply kept in readiness
core_image: 仓库深处留着一批物资，标签上写着「备用」
scene: 他们在车库后面留了几箱水，以备停电时使用。 They reserved several boxes of water behind the garage in case the power failed.
sceneCN: 这里 reserve 是「保留」（第 1 个义项：留作以后使用）；句意：他们在车库后面留了几箱水，以备停电时使用。

derivatives.zh: 预订；保留意见
矜持的；保留的
预备役军人

senses.title: To keep for future use
senses.definition: to keep something so that it can be used later
senses.definitionCN: 把某物留存下来，供以后使用
senses.example: They reserved several boxes of water behind the garage.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车库后面留了几箱水。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to keep back, which is the core of every sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为保留，这是所有义项的核心。

senses.title: A supply kept ready
senses.definition: an amount of something kept for use in an emergency or later
senses.definitionCN: 为紧急情况或以后使用而储存的数量
senses.example: The army kept a reserve of fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 军队储备了燃料。
senses.why: The noun names the thing that has been kept back.
senses.whyCN: 名词指被保留下来的东西。

senses.title: Self-restraint
senses.definition: the habit of not showing feelings or thoughts openly
senses.definitionCN: 不轻易外露情感或想法的习惯
senses.example: He spoke with reserve about his own success.
senses.exampleCN: 他谈到自己的成功时很克制。
senses.why: Feelings kept back from view produce the social sense of reserve.
senses.whyCN: 情感被留在视线之外，就产生「矜持」这一社交含义。

intro.en: Reserve comes from Latin reservare, to keep back, from re- and servare, to keep, through Old French reserver.
intro.cn: reserve 来自拉丁语 reservare（保留），由 re- 与 servare（保存）构成，经古法语 reserver 进入英语。

items.en: Servare means to keep or preserve.
items.cn: servare 意为保存、保全。

items.en: Reservare means to keep back for later.
items.cn: reservare 意为留到以后。

items.en: Reserver means to reserve or hold back.
items.cn: reserver 意为保留、扣下。

items.en: Middle English reserven means to keep back.
items.cn: 中古英语 reserven 意为保留。

items.en: Reserve appears as a noun for a supply kept ready.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，reserve 作为名词出现，指备用的储备。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of personal restraint.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「个人克制」这一义项。

note.en: Reserve is a keeping-back word, and it sits near its family and near verbs for keeping and booking.
note.cn: reserve 是一个「留住」词，与自身词族以及表示保存和预订的动词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Reserve is re- plus the Latin root for keep: to keep something back for later.
normalIntro.cn: reserve 是 re- 加拉丁语「保存」词根：把东西留到以后。

normal.en: Reserve a table means keep it for a future time.
normal.cn: reserve a table 意为把桌子留到以后用。

normal.en: A nature reserve is land kept for wildlife.
normal.cn: nature reserve 是为野生动物保留的土地。

normal.en: In reserve means held ready but not yet used.
normal.cn: in reserve 意为留作备用、尚未使用。

normal.en: Reserved can describe a quiet, restrained person.
normal.cn: reserved 可以形容安静、克制的人。

normal.en: Compare keep: keep is general, while reserve stresses setting aside.
normal.cn: 对比 keep：keep 更泛，reserve 强调「单独留出来」。

abstract.en: Picture boxes stacked at the back of a garage.
abstract.cn: 想象车库深处堆着几只箱子。

abstract.en: Imagine a fuel gauge with a hidden lower section.
abstract.cn: 想象油表下面还藏着一段备用油量。

abstract.en: Think of a quiet person holding words back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个安静的人把话留在心里。

examples.en: Please reserve a table for two.
examples.cn: 请订一张两人桌。

examples.en: They reserved several boxes of water behind the garage.

examples.en: The nature reserve protects rare birds.
examples.cn: 自然保护区保护稀有鸟类。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + serve」——留下来以后再用，就是保留；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 servare（保存）→ reservare（保留）→ 古法语 reserver → 中古英语 reserven → 现代英语 reserve，核心义「留住备用」。

sensesIntro.en: The word keeps one image, holding something back: a thing kept for later, a supply set aside, and feelings kept out of sight.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终保留一个意象——把东西留住：留待以后之物、单列出来的储备，以及不外露的情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a supply set aside with a label saying for later.
core.cn: 核心意象：一批物资被单独放好，标签写着「留待以后」。

branches.en: Keeping something for later is the core verb sense.
branches.cn: 留作后用，是核心动词义项。

branches.en: A reserve is the supply that has been set aside.
branches.cn: 储备就是被单独留出的物资。

branches.en: Reserve of manner is feeling kept back from view.
branches.cn: 举止上的矜持，是情感被留在视线之外。

branches.en: The act of reserving creates the thing held in reserve.
branches.cn: 保留的行为造出了储备之物。

branches.en: A hidden supply and hidden feeling share the same restraint.
branches.cn: 隐藏的物资与隐藏的情感共享同一种克制。

intro.cn: reserve 是经法语改造的拉丁动词，现代词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin servare means to keep, and reservare means to keep back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 servare 意为保存，reservare 意为保留。

items.example: Re- adds the idea of keeping back.

definition_zh: 前进；推进；进展；晋升；提出；预付；前进的步伐；上涨
definition_en: to move forward, to make progress, to raise to a higher rank, to put forward an idea, or to pay money before it is due
core_image: 一队人顶着风朝雾里迈步，最前面的那一排最先被雾吞掉
scene: 雨夜里，队伍沿山脊缓慢向前，探路的灯在雾里忽明忽暗。 The column advanced along the ridge without a sound.
sceneCN: 这里 advance 指队伍在地面上向前移动（第 1 个义项：向前挺进）；句意为队伍沿着山脊悄无声息地前进。

pos.zh: 动词：前进；推进；进展；晋升；提出；预付
名词：前进；进展；预付款；上涨

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「推进；进步；晋升」
由本词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「高级的；先进的；晚期的」
由本词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「前进的；发展中的」

senses.title: To move forward on the ground
senses.definition: to move forward, especially as a group or a body of troops moving towards a place
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动，尤指队伍或军队朝某地推进
senses.example: The troops advanced through the valley at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 部队在黎明时穿过山谷推进。
senses.why: The Latin element ante means before or in front, so to advance is literally to put the body in front of the point it held.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语成分 ante 意为「在前面」，所以 advance 字面上就是把身体放到原先位置的前方。

senses.title: To make progress or develop
senses.definition: to develop, improve, or move to a higher stage, as knowledge, technology, or a plan does
senses.definitionCN: 指知识、技术或计划等发展、改善，进入更高阶段
senses.example: Research on batteries has advanced faster than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 电池研究的发展比预期更快。
senses.why: Progress is forward motion applied to something abstract; the same image of reaching the front is moved from feet to knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 进展是把「向前移动」用在抽象事物上；同一个「跑到最前面」的画面，从脚步移到了知识上。

senses.title: To rise to a higher rank
senses.definition: to raise someone to a higher position or rank, or to rise to one
senses.definitionCN: 把某人提到更高的职位或等级，或本人升到更高位置
senses.example: She was advanced to head of the department after two years.
senses.exampleCN: 两年后她被提升为部门主管。
senses.why: Standing at the front of a formation is both a place and a rank, so the spatial idea of moving forward became the social idea of promotion.
senses.whyCN: 站在队列前排既是位置，也是等级；于是「向前移动」这个空间概念就变成了「晋升」这个社会概念。

senses.title: To put forward an idea
senses.definition: to suggest or present an idea, plan, or theory for other people to consider
senses.definitionCN: 提出想法、计划或理论，供他人考虑
senses.example: The engineer advanced a simple fix for the leaking pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师为漏水的管道提出了一个简单的修补办法。
senses.why: To set something in front of people is to lay it on the table for discussion, so being in front turns into being proposed.
senses.whyCN: 把东西摆到众人前面，就是把它放到桌面上供人讨论；「在前」于是转成了「提出」。

senses.title: To pay money before it is due
senses.definition: to pay or lend money before it is owed or before the usual time
senses.definitionCN: 在应付之前或通常时间之前付出或借出钱款
senses.example: The publisher advanced her a sum against future sales.
senses.exampleCN: 出版商预支给她一笔钱，以后从销售中扣除。
senses.why: Money that arrives before the goods is like a runner who reaches the front early; the forward image is simply transferred to payment.
senses.whyCN: 钱比货物先到，就像一个提前跑到前面的人；「向前」的画面就这样被搬到了付款上。

senses.title: Forward movement or a step of progress
senses.definition: noun: forward movement, or a step of progress or improvement
senses.definitionCN: 名词，指向前的移动，或进展、改进的一步
senses.example: Recent advances in printing have cut the cost of small runs.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷术近来的进步降低了小批量印刷的成本。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical picture intact: an advance is one step taken to the front, whether with the feet or in a field of study.
senses.whyCN: 名词完整保留了那个身体画面：advance 就是朝前迈出的一步，不论用脚走还是在某个领域里走。

senses.title: Money paid ahead of time
senses.definition: noun: money paid before it is earned or before the agreed time, often as a loan or a first instalment
senses.definitionCN: 名词，指在挣得之前或约定时间之前付出的钱，常为借款或首期款
senses.example: He asked for a cash advance on his salary.
senses.exampleCN: 他申请预支一部分工资现金。
senses.why: The noun can also name the thing that arrives early: the money itself stands in front of the work it is meant to pay for.
senses.whyCN: 名词也可以指那件「早到」的东西：钱本身站到了它本该偿付的活儿前面。

senses.title: To rise in price or value
senses.definition: of prices, shares, or amounts, to rise to a higher level
senses.definitionCN: 指价格、股票或数额上升到更高水平
senses.example: Shares advanced three percent after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告发布后股价上涨了百分之三。
senses.why: On a price chart, going up is drawn as moving to the right, so a rising line is literally a line that advances.
senses.whyCN: 在价格图表上，「向上」被画成向右延伸，所以一条上涨的线字面上就是一条向前推进的线。

intro.en: Advance came into English from Old French, and the older source is generally traced to Latin abante, 'from in front'.
intro.cn: advance 从古法语进入英语，更早的来源一般认为可追溯到拉丁语 abante，意为「从前面」。

items.en: Ante meant 'before, in front of', and it supplies the forward direction of the whole family.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前、在前面」，为这一族词提供了「向前」的方向。

items.en: Ab 'from' plus ante formed abante, 'from before, in front'. The form is late, and how far it was used in everyday speech is source uncertain.
items.cn: ab「从」加 ante 构成 abante，意为「从前面」。这个形式出现较晚，它在日常口语中用得多广，来源不确定。

items.en: Old French avancer meant 'to move forward, to push forward, to promote'; the loss of the b and the new ending are French developments.
items.cn: 古法语 avancer 意为「向前移动、推进、提升」；b 的脱落与新的词尾都是法语自身的变化。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as avancen in the thirteenth century; the noun advance appears later, built on the same French stem.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入动词形式 avancen；名词 advance 出现较晚，建立在同一个法语词干上。

items.en: Commercial and financial uses grew in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries: to advance money, a cash advance, and prices advancing in the market.
items.cn: 商业与金融用法在十八、十九世纪发展起来：advance money、cash advance，以及市场上的价格上涨。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same French stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for moving ahead, improving, promoting and paying early.
note.cn: 形近组都由同一个法语词干构成；近义组收表示向前、进步、提升与提前付款的词。
