entries.definition: At a high level or stage; also the past form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「高级的、先进的、晚期的」，同时是动词的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: Moving forward or developing; the present participle of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或现在分词，义为「前进的、发展中的」。

entries.definition: A related noun from the same French element avant, but it branched off to mean a favourable position.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优势」，与本词同出古法语 avant「在前」，但已分化为表示有利位置的另一支。

entries.definition: To go on or move forward, often after a stop; more formal and less military.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「继续进行、前往」，常指停顿之后继续，语体更正式，军事色彩更弱。

entries.definition: To move forward or improve over time, stressing steady development rather than one step.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「前进、进展」，强调持续的逐步发展，而非单次迈步。

entries.definition: To move someone to a higher rank or position; the usual word for a job.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提升、晋升」，是谈职位升迁时最常用的词。

entries.definition: To help something develop or succeed; a formal verb close to the supporting sense of advance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「促进、推动」，语气正式，接近 advance 表示支持某事的那层意思。

entries.definition: Money lent, often the everyday word for a sum advanced to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「贷款、借出」，常是预支给某人一笔钱时的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin element ante and the everyday phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语成分 ante，以及这个词日常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ante is 'before, in front', so whatever advances goes to the front of where it was.
normal.cn: ante 是「在前面」，所以任何 advance 都是跑到原先位置的前方。

normal.en: Old French avancer already meant both to move forward and to promote, so the job sense is old, not modern.
normal.cn: 古法语 avancer 已经同时表示「向前」与「提升」，所以晋升义由来已久，并非现代才有。

normal.en: In advance means the ticket, the warning or the money arrives before the thing itself.
normal.cn: in advance 指票、警告或钱比事情本身先到。

normal.en: An advance on a salary is money that runs ahead of the work it pays for.
normal.cn: an advance on a salary 就是跑到活儿前面的钱。

normal.en: On a chart the line advances to the right, which is why shares can advance.
normal.cn: 图表上的线向右推进，所以股票也可以用 advance 表示上涨。

abstract.en: Picture a column of soldiers stepping into fog: the front of the line keeps vanishing, and the back keeps filling the gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一队士兵走进雾里：队伍最前面不断消失，后面的人不断补上。

abstract.en: Every advance is a small trade, leaving a known spot for one you cannot see yet.
abstract.cn: 每一次前进都是一次小交换：离开熟悉的位置，走向还看不见的地方。

abstract.en: The same step forward can be a march, a discovery, a promotion or a payment made early; only the direction stays the same.
abstract.cn: 同一个向前的动作可以是行军、发现、升职或提前付款，不变的只有方向。

examples.en: The troops advanced through the valley at dawn.
examples.cn: 部队在黎明时穿过山谷推进。

examples.en: Research on batteries has advanced faster than expected.
examples.cn: 电池研究的发展比预期更快。

examples.en: He asked for a cash advance on his salary.
examples.cn: 他申请预支一部分工资现金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德万斯」——阿德把车往前一推，轮子先滚到前头：前进、推进。

root: 古法语 avancer「向前移动、推进、提升」，更早一般认为出自拉丁语 abante「从前面」，由 ab「从」+ ante「在前」构成。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all come from one gesture, putting something in front: a body, a project, a rank, an idea, a sum of money, a price.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都出自同一个动作——把东西放到前面：身体、工程、职位、想法、钱款、价格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people stepping forward into fog, the front edge always the first to enter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人朝雾里迈步，最前面的边缘总是最先进入。

branches.en: THE BODY: a group moves to the front of the ground it occupies.
branches.cn: 身体线：队伍朝所占地面之前移动。

branches.en: THE PROJECT: forward motion becomes progress, and the noun names that single step.
branches.cn: 工程线：向前的动作变成进展，名词就指那迈出的一步。

branches.en: THE LADDER: standing at the front of a formation turns into standing higher in rank.
branches.cn: 阶梯线：站到队列前排，转成职位上的升高。

branches.en: THE TABLE: an idea is set in front of others so that they can examine it.
branches.cn: 桌面线：把想法摆到别人面前供人审视。

branches.en: THE MONEY: cash, wages and prices can all arrive early or move higher than the usual point.
branches.cn: 钱款线：现金、工资和价格都可以比通常的时点更早到达或走高。

intro.en: Advance is a French verb rebuilt in English; its parts are the Latin elements ab- and ante plus a French ending.
intro.cn: advance 是英语中重塑的法语动词；它的成分是拉丁语 ab- 与 ante，再加上法语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ab, ante and abante are recorded forms; the deeper Indo-European origin of ante is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ab、ante 与 abante 都是有记录的形式；ante 更早的印欧语来源属于重构。

items.example: It is the first element of abante.
items.exampleCN: 它是 abante 的第一个成分。

items.example: Ante gives the forward direction of the word.
items.exampleCN: ante 提供这个词「向前」的方向。

items.example: Abante is the generally accepted older source of the French verb.
items.exampleCN: abante 一般认为就是那个法语动词的更早来源。

items.example: French kept avant where Latin had ante.
items.exampleCN: 法语用 avant 承接了拉丁语的 ante。

items.example: English borrowed this verb as advance.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个动词借来作 advance。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「推进；进步；晋升」
由本词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「高级的；先进的」
由本词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「前进的；发展中的」

definition_zh: 执照；许可证；许可；准许；放纵；艺术上的特许自由
definition_en: an official document that allows an activity, formal permission to do something, or the freedom to behave beyond the usual limits
core_image: 一张盖了章的纸压在柜台玻璃下，边角已经被翻得发软
scene: 卡车在检查站停下，司机从手套箱里取出一张对折的纸，递给窗外的检查员。 The officer checked the licence before the truck moved on.
sceneCN: 这里是「执照、许可证」（第 1 个义项：官方发放的证件）；句意为检查员看过执照之后才放卡车继续走。图中可辨识物件：检查站、对折的纸、卡车车窗。

pos.zh: 执照；许可证；许可；准许；放纵；特许自由

collocations.zh: 杀人的特许；行事不受追究的许可

derivatives.zh: 英式名词写作 licence，美式名词与动词都写作 license；动词义为「批准；发许可证给」
由 license 加 -ed 构成，义为「获得许可的；持照的」
由 license 加 -ee 构成，义为「获得许可的人；持照人」
由 license 加 -ure 构成，义为「许可的授予；执照制度」

senses.title: An official document that allows an activity
senses.definition: a document issued by an authority that gives a person or a business the right to do something
senses.definitionCN: 由主管机关发放、赋予个人或企业做某事的权利的证件
senses.example: He showed his driving licence to the officer.
senses.exampleCN: 他把驾驶执照出示给警官。
senses.why: Latin licentia named permission, and a licence is that permission made visible as paper, so the abstract right and the card in a wallet are the same sense at two stages.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 licentia 指的就是许可，而 licence 是把那份许可变成看得见的纸；因此抽象的权利与钱包里的卡片，是同一个义项的两个阶段。

senses.title: Formal permission to do something
senses.definition: official or formal permission, whether or not it comes with a document
senses.definitionCN: 正式或官方的准许，无论是否附有证件
senses.example: The film was shown under licence from the studio.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影获得制片公司许可后才放映。
senses.why: Strip away the paper and what remains is the permission itself; the word then names the granting rather than the certificate.
senses.whyCN: 把纸去掉，剩下的就是许可本身；此时这个词指的是「准许」这件行为，而不是那张证书。

senses.title: Freedom to behave beyond the usual limits
senses.definition: the freedom to act without restraint, often used when the freedom has gone too far
senses.definitionCN: 不受约束地行事的自由，常用于指这种自由已经过了头
senses.example: The novel's licence with facts annoyed historians.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说对史实的随意处理让历史学家不满。
senses.why: Permission with no one setting its edges turns into boldness; the same noun slides from an allowed act to an excess that others resent.
senses.whyCN: 一旦没有人给许可划边界，准许就变成大胆妄为；同一个名词从「被允许的行为」滑向「让别人不满的过头」。

senses.title: Special freedom granted to an artist or writer
senses.definition: the accepted freedom of a writer or artist to change facts or break rules for effect
senses.definitionCN: 作家或艺术家为效果而改动事实、打破常规时被认可的自由
senses.example: Poetic licence let the songwriter bend the grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 诗歌的特许自由让这位词作者改动了语法。
senses.why: The narrowest sense is a professional allowance: art is permitted to depart from fact, and the word keeps the same frame of granted freedom.
senses.whyCN: 最窄的义项是一种职业上的照顾：艺术被允许偏离事实，而这个词仍然保留「被授予的自由」这一框架。

intro.en: Licence comes from a Latin verb for being allowed, through its abstract noun, and the noun arrived in English by way of French with the sense of leave or permission.
intro.cn: licence 来自拉丁语中表示「被允许」的动词，经它的抽象名词，再由法语以「准许、许可」的意思进入英语。

items.en: Licere meant to be allowed or to be permitted, and it described what a person might lawfully do.
items.cn: licere 意为被允许、获准，描述一个人可以合法地做什么。

items.en: Licentia was the noun for freedom or permission, and it could also name boldness that oversteps.
items.cn: licentia 是表示自由或许可的名词，也可以指越界的大胆。

items.en: Old French took the noun as licence, meaning leave or permission, and handed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词作 licence，意为准许或许可，并传给了英语。

items.en: Middle English licence covers a granted privilege, a formal permission and the freedom of behaviour.
items.cn: 中古英语的 licence 覆盖被授予的特权、正式的许可，以及行为上的自由。

items.en: Modern English keeps licence as the British noun and license as the American spelling, while the verb is license everywhere.
items.cn: 现代英语保留英式名词 licence 与美式拼写 license，而动词在各地都写作 license。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the spelling variants and the Latin relatives of the permit word; the near-meaning group collects words for documents and for freedom.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的拼写变体与拉丁同族；近义组收表示证件与自由的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the noun, and the verb spelling used everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词的美式拼写，也是各地通用的动词拼写。

entries.definition: Holding an official permission.
entries.definitionCN: 持有官方许可的；持照的。

entries.definition: A person who holds a licence.
entries.definitionCN: 持有执照的人；获许可者。

entries.definition: A person holding a formal qualification, from the Latin stem of permission.
entries.definitionCN: 持有正式资格的人，来自拉丁语中表示许可的词干。

entries.definition: An official document allowing something.
entries.definitionCN: 允许做某事的官方文件。

entries.definition: The act of allowing something to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某事发生的行为。

entries.definition: The state of being free to act.
entries.definitionCN: 可以自由行动的状态。

entries.definition: A formal document granting rights.
entries.definitionCN: 授予权利的正式文件。

normalIntro.en: A Latin verb for being allowed supplies the stem, its noun adds the idea of freedom, and English splits the spelling between the noun and the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「被允许」的动词提供词干，它的名词加上「自由」的含义，英语又在名词与动词之间分出拼写。

normal.en: Licere is Latin for to be allowed, and licentia is the permission that it grants.
normal.cn: licere 是拉丁语的「被允许」，licentia 是它给出的许可。

normal.en: British English keeps licence for the noun and license for the verb; American English uses license for both.
normal.cn: 英式英语名词用 licence、动词用 license；美式英语两者都用 license。

normal.en: The c sounds like an s, and the ending rhymes with fence.
normal.cn: 其中的 c 读作 s，词尾与 fence 押韵。

normal.en: The -ee in licensee marks the receiver, while the giver is the licensor.
normal.cn: licensee 里的 -ee 标记接受者，给出许可的一方则是 licensor。

normal.en: Poetic licence is a fixed phrase for the freedom to break rules in art.
normal.cn: poetic licence 是固定说法，指艺术中打破规则的自由。

abstract.en: A licence is permission turned into paper, so a right can be carried in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 执照是把许可变成纸，于是一项权利可以被装进口袋。

abstract.en: The same noun covers a permit and an excess of freedom, because both begin from permission.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词既指许可证，也指过度的自由，因为两者都从「许可」出发。

abstract.en: Every licence draws a line: it says what may be done and quietly says what may not.
abstract.cn: 每一张执照都划出一条线：它写明可以做什么，也悄悄写明不可以做什么。

examples.en: He showed his driving licence to the officer.
examples.cn: 他把驾驶执照出示给警官。

examples.en: The film was shown under licence from the studio.
examples.cn: 这部电影获得制片公司许可后才放映。

examples.en: Poetic licence let the songwriter bend the grammar.
examples.cn: 诗歌的特许自由让这位词作者改动了语法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来 sense」——领执照得讲常识；licence 是许可证。

root: 拉丁语 licere（被允许）→ 名词 licentia（许可、自由）→ 古法语 licence → 英语；英式名词作 licence，美式名词与动词均作 license。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a granted permission, first as a stamped document, then as the permission itself, and finally as freedom that has slipped past its limits.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被授予的许可：先是一张盖章的证件，再是许可本身，最后是越过边界的自由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped sheet of paper held under the glass of a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张盖了章的纸压在柜台的玻璃下面。

branches.en: a folded card handed through a truck window
branches.cn: 从卡车车窗递出的对折卡片

branches.en: a studio letter allowing a screening
branches.cn: 制片公司允许放映的一封信

branches.en: a novel taking liberties with the record
branches.cn: 一部随意改动史实的小说

branches.en: a lyric that breaks grammar on purpose
branches.cn: 故意打破语法的歌词

branches.en: one permission seen as paper and as consent
branches.cn: 同一份许可的纸上形态与口头同意

intro.en: A Latin verb of permission, its abstract noun, a French reshaping, and two English endings for the receiver and the act keep this word in place.
intro.cn: 一个表示许可的拉丁动词、它的抽象名词、一次法语改写，以及两个标记接受者与动作的英语词尾，把这个词固定下来。

latinIntro.en: Licere, licentia and licitus are recorded Latin words, so the permission family has a firm Latin base.
latinIntro.cn: licere、licentia 与 licitus 都是有记录的拉丁词，这一族「许可」有坚实的拉丁语基础。

items.meaning: the person who receives a licence

definition_zh: 大约；粗略地；粗暴地
definition_en: approximately, without detail, or in a harsh way
core_image: 用眼睛估出来的一段距离
scene: 从车站到旅馆大约要走十分钟。 It takes roughly ten minutes to walk from the station to the hotel.
sceneCN: 这里 roughly 是「大约」（第 1 个义项）；句意：从车站到旅馆大约要走十分钟。

derivatives.zh: 粗糙的；粗略的
粗糙；粗鲁
使变粗糙

senses.title: Approximately
senses.definition: used to give a number or amount that is not exact
senses.definitionCN: 用于给出并不精确的数字或数量
senses.example: The trip costs roughly fifty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行大约花五十英镑。
senses.why: The figure is rubbed smooth only at the edges.
senses.whyCN: 数字只在边缘被粗略磨平。

senses.title: Without detail
senses.definition: in a way that is not detailed or careful
senses.definitionCN: 以不细致、不周密的方式
senses.example: He roughly described the route on a napkin.
senses.exampleCN: 他在餐巾纸上粗略画了路线。
senses.why: The outline is left rough, without fine work.
senses.whyCN: 轮廓留得粗糙，没有细加工。

senses.title: Harshly
senses.definition: in a rough or unkind way
senses.definitionCN: 以粗暴或不友善的方式
senses.example: The guard spoke roughly to the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫对人群说话很粗暴。
senses.why: A rough manner hurts like a rough surface.
senses.whyCN: 粗暴的态度像粗糙表面一样伤人。

intro.en: Roughly is rough plus -ly, in a rough manner.
intro.cn: roughly 由 rough 加 -ly 构成，意为以粗糙的方式。

items.en: Ruh means uneven or coarse.
items.cn: ruh 意为不平的或粗糙的。

items.en: Rough keeps the uneven sense.
items.cn: rough 保留不平整的含义。

items.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.en: Roughly often marks an approximate number.
items.cn: roughly 常用来标记近似数字。

items.en: Roughly speaking becomes a common phrase.
items.cn: roughly speaking 成为常用短语。

note.en: Roughly gives an estimate; harshly describes bad treatment.
note.cn: roughly 表示估计，harshly 则描述恶劣对待。

entries.definition: not smooth or exact
entries.definitionCN: 粗糙的；粗略的

entries.definition: to disturb a smooth surface
entries.definitionCN: 弄皱；扰乱

entries.definition: a frilled collar
entries.definitionCN: 轮状皱领

entries.definition: approximately
entries.definitionCN: 大约

entries.definition: close to an exact number
entries.definitionCN: 近似地

entries.definition: in a severe way
entries.definitionCN: 严厉地；粗暴地

normalIntro.en: Roughly puts a rough edge on numbers and manners.
normalIntro.cn: roughly 给数字和态度都加上一层粗糙的边。

normal.en: The journey takes roughly two hours.
normal.cn: 这段路程大约要两小时。

normal.en: Roughly speaking, half the class agreed.
normal.cn: 粗略地说，班里一半人同意。

normal.en: The two boxes are roughly equal in weight.
normal.cn: 两个箱子重量大致相等。

normal.en: He roughly sketched the plan on paper.
normal.cn: 他在纸上粗略画了计划。

normal.en: Do not treat the old books roughly.
normal.cn: 不要粗暴对待这些旧书。

abstract.en: Picture a hand measuring a distance by eye.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手用眼睛估量距离。

abstract.en: Imagine a pencil outline drawn in a hurry.
abstract.cn: 想象匆忙画出的铅笔轮廓。

abstract.en: Think of a door pushed open without care.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被粗鲁地推开。

examples.en: There are roughly thirty people in the hall.
examples.cn: 大厅里大约有三十人。

examples.en: She roughly folded the map and left.
examples.cn: 她粗略地折起地图就走了。

examples.en: The prisoners were treated roughly.
examples.cn: 囚犯们受到了粗暴对待。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rough（粗）＋ ly」——数字算得粗就是大约；事情做得粗就是粗略；待人粗就是粗暴。

root: rough（粗糙的）＋ -ly（以…方式）→ roughly，核心义「以粗而不精的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Roughly means approximately, without detail, or in a harsh way.
sensesIntro.cn: roughly 意为大约、粗略地，或以粗暴的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a distance measured by eye.
core.cn: 核心意象：用眼睛估量的距离。

branches.en: Approximate numbers are the first sense.
branches.cn: 近似数字是第一个义项。

branches.en: Work done without detail is rough work.
branches.cn: 不细致的工作就是粗略的。

branches.en: Rough manners become harsh treatment.
branches.cn: 粗糙的态度变成粗暴对待。

branches.en: Both leave precision aside.
branches.cn: 两者都舍弃了精确。

branches.en: The same word covers numbers and behavior.
branches.cn: 同一个词涵盖数字与行为。

intro.en: Roughly is the adverb built from rough.
intro.cn: roughly 是由 rough 构成的副词。

latinIntro.en: Roughly has no Latin root; it is English throughout.
latinIntro.cn: roughly 没有拉丁词根，完全来自英语。

definition_zh: 堆；一堆； pile ；堆放；桩；柱；涌出
definition_en: objects lying one on another in a mass, or to put things in such a mass, or a heavy column driven into the ground
core_image: 东西一件压一件，越叠越高，摇摇欲坠
scene: 搬家那天，妈妈把书一本一本摞在门口，摞到快有人那么高。 The books stood in a tall pile by the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「堆；一堆」（第 1 个义项：叠在一起的物品）；句意为书摞成高高的一堆立在门口。画面里就是一摞顶到下巴的书。

pos.zh: 堆放；堆叠；（pile) （非正式）涌进涌出

derivatives.zh: pile 加 -ing 构成，义为「打桩；桩群」
pile 与 up 的复合形容词，义为「堆积的」
与 pile 同源的姊妹词形，义为「塔架；桥塔」

senses.title: A mass of things lying one on another
senses.definition: objects stacked loosely on top of each other
senses.definitionCN: 松散地叠在一起的物品
senses.example: A pile of letters waited on his desk.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆信件堆在他的桌上等处理。
senses.why: Latin pila meant a pier or column, and the stone sense became the picture for things resting on each other.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pila 指桥墩或柱，石头意象变成了东西彼此叠压的画面。

senses.title: A large quantity
senses.definition: a very large amount of something, especially money
senses.definitionCN: 很大数量，尤指金钱
senses.example: She made a pile selling handmade jewellery online.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠网上卖手工首饰赚了一大笔。
senses.why: A stack grows until it becomes abundance: the picture of many objects turns into the idea of much.
senses.whyCN: 一堆东西越堆越多，直到变成「丰盛」：从许多件东西的画面转出「大量」的概念。

senses.title: A heavy column driven into the ground
senses.definition: a long heavy beam of wood, steel or concrete driven into the ground to support a building
senses.definitionCN: 打入地下的木、钢或混凝土长柱，用于支撑建筑
senses.example: Workers drove a concrete pile into the riverbed.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把一根混凝土桩打进河床。
senses.why: This sense keeps the original Latin image of a pier standing on stone: a column holding weight.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了拉丁语原意中「石上立柱」的形象：一根承重的柱。

senses.title: To put things in a heap
senses.definition: to put things on top of each other in a loose mass
senses.definitionCN: 把东西松散地叠放在一起
senses.example: He piled the dirty dishes beside the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 他把脏盘子堆在水槽边。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb by conversion: to make a pile out of things.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接转类成动词：把东西弄成一堆。

senses.title: To move quickly in a crowd
senses.titleCN: 涌进涌出（pile into / out of）
senses.definition: to move quickly and in large numbers into or out of a place
senses.definitionCN: 大量的人快速涌进或涌出某处
senses.example: The team piled out of the bus and onto the field.
senses.exampleCN: 全队从车上涌出来跑向球场。
senses.why: People pressed together like objects in a heap, so the heap picture covers movement too.
senses.whyCN: 人们挤在一起，就像堆里的东西，堆的画面也覆盖了移动。

senses.title: To accumulate over time
senses.definition: to increase gradually until there are too many
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐增加直到多到应付不过来
senses.example: Unpaid bills piled up during her illness.
senses.exampleCN: 她生病期间未付的账单越积越多。
senses.why: One object on another, day after day, until the heap can no longer be managed.
senses.whyCN: 一件压一件，日复一日，直到那堆东西再也无法应付。

senses.title: To add pressure or blame
senses.definition: to add more criticism, work or pressure to what already exists
senses.definitionCN: 在已有基础上追加批评、工作或压力
senses.example: The tabloids piled on after the scandal broke.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻曝光后小报们火上浇油。
senses.why: Adding one more thing to a heap is exactly what a critic does to a reputation.
senses.whyCN: 往堆上再添一件东西，正是批评者对名声做的事。

intro.en: Pile comes through Old French from Latin pila, a pier or column of stone; the heap meaning grew from the column picture, and modern building took the column back as a technical sense.
intro.cn: pile 经古法语来自拉丁语 pila（石桥墩或柱）；「堆」义从柱子的形象长出来，而现代建筑又把「柱」收回去当专业义项。

items.en: Pila meant a stone pillar or a mole built into the sea.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pila 指石柱或伸入海中的堤。

items.en: Pile kept the column meaning as it passed into French.
items.cn: 进入法语后 pile 保留了柱子的意思。

items.en: English took pile for both the column and, by image, the heap of things stacked like stones.
items.cn: 英语借入 pile，既指柱子，也借其形象指像石头一样叠起来的堆。

items.en: Engineering revived the column as a beam driven into soil to carry weight.
items.cn: 工程学把柱义复活为打入土中承重的桩。

items.en: Informal English made a pile for making a fortune and pile up for bills and debts accumulating.
items.cn: 非正式英语用 make a pile 指发大财，用 pile up 指账单债务的累积。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the Latin column family and a false friend; the near-meaning group holds words for heaps and stacking.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁「柱」词族和一个假朋友；近义组收指堆与叠放的词。

entries.definition: A tall upright column supporting a building or a person's role.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑建筑或承担角色的立柱。

entries.definition: A tower carrying cables or marking a road, from the same Latin stone image.
entries.definitionCN: 承载线缆或标示道路的塔架，源于同一拉丁石柱意象。

entries.definition: A structure from shore into water; spelling looks close but the source differs.
entries.definitionCN: 从岸边伸入水中的结构；拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: A disorderly mass of things thrown together.
entries.definitionCN: 乱扔在一起的杂乱一堆。

entries.definition: A neatly arranged pile, often of the same items.
entries.definitionCN: 码放整齐的一叠，通常是同类物品。

entries.definition: A rounded heap of earth or small objects.
entries.definitionCN: 土或小物件的圆堆。

normalIntro.en: The word hides two pictures — a stack of things and a column of stone — and both help memory.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词藏着两幅画面——一堆东西和一根石柱——都有助于记忆。

normal.en: Latin pila, stone pillar; picture a pillar of books standing on the desk.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pila 是石柱；想象桌上一摞立起来的书柱。

normal.en: Pile up works for laundry, bills and snow: anything that grows one layer at a time.
normal.cn: pile up 可用于脏衣、账单和积雪：任何一层层长起来的东西。

normal.en: Pile into the car keeps the heap picture: bodies squeezed like luggage.
normal.cn: pile into the car 保留堆的画面：人像行李一样挤在一起。

normal.en: Make a pile is British money slang — a pile of banknotes, not of stones.
normal.cn: make a pile 是英式金钱俚语——指的是一叠钞票，不是石头。

normal.en: A foundation pile goes down, a laundry pile goes up — one word, two directions.
normal.cn: 地基桩往下打，脏衣堆往上摞——一个词，两个方向。

abstract.en: Gravity does the stacking: things fall onto things, and a pile is born.
abstract.cn: 重力完成堆叠：东西落在东西上，一堆就诞生了。

abstract.en: A debt grows invisibly, but a pile grows visibly — the word forces you to see the burden.
abstract.cn: 债务无形地生长，堆却看得见——这个词逼你看见负担。

abstract.en: From stone pier to paper stack, pile measures everything that holds something up by mass.
abstract.cn: 从石墩到纸堆，pile 丈量一切靠体量托住东西的东西。

examples.en: She sorted the washing into three piles.
examples.cn: 她把要洗的衣服分成三堆。

examples.en: Work kept piling up before the holidays.
examples.cn: 假期之前工作越积越多。

examples.en: The bridge rests on concrete piles sunk deep in mud.
examples.cn: 大桥坐落在深插泥中的混凝土桩上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派哦」——快递员派件派哦，门口堆成小山；pile 就是一堆。

root: 拉丁语 pila（石柱、堤）经古法语 pile 进入中古英语；「堆」义由石柱叠石的形象引申，工程义「桩」则保留柱的本义。

sensesIntro.en: A single stone image forks into two lines: the vertical column that carries a building, and the loose heap that anything falling makes.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个石头的意象分出两条线：承载建筑的竖直柱，和任何东西落下时形成的那堆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: things resting one on another, whether stacked by hands or sunk by machines.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件压着一件，无论是人手摞的还是机器打的。

branches.en: letters lying on a desk in layers
branches.cn: 一层层躺在桌上的信件

branches.en: banknotes counted in thick stacks
branches.cn: 厚厚一叠一叠数着的钞票

branches.en: a beam disappearing into river mud
branches.cn: 一根没入河泥的桩柱

branches.en: players squeezing through one door
branches.cn: 球员们从一扇门里挤出来

branches.en: the same heap, made in a minute or a year
branches.cn: 同一堆东西，一分钟或一年堆成

intro.en: Pile itself is unanalysable, but English builds freely on it with particles and compounds.
intro.cn: pile 本身不可再分析，但英语用小词和复合词在它上面自由构词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root pila left few direct relatives in English; most of the family was built inside English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 pila 在英语里留下的直接同源词不多；词族大部分在英语内部构成。
